# Closed Feedback Archive (Build Session writes, Design Session reads)

This file is owned exclusively by the **Build Session** alongside `docs/FEEDBACK.md`.

When `docs/FEEDBACK.md` approaches the 300-line / 25 KB doc limit, the Build Session moves `answered` or `closed` feedback items (`FB-nn`) and superseded build logs from `docs/FEEDBACK.md` into this archive file. `tools/fc.sh docs` skips `docs/archive/`.

## FB-01 to FB-22 (moved 2026-11-07)

### FB-01: BASERULES1-M points at the wrong sections

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` section 1 row 4; `docs/specs/BASERULES1.md`
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: The row says to build from `BASERULES1.md` "sections 1-2 only". Those sections describe today's rules and their weaknesses. The register metadata, `check/ruleset.rs`, bundle tests and `aegis rules` with `LOCKED` and `--contract` are specified in `BASERULES1.md` section 6 ("How the engine enforces it") and its section 7 row BASERULES1-M, and in `BASERULES1_LIBRARY.md` (the option table, bundles, and section 7's authoring note).
- **Recommendation**: Point the row at `BASERULES1.md` sections 6-7 and `BASERULES1_LIBRARY.md`. Until answered, the build follows the row's own summary and acceptance test, which match section 6.

### FB-03: The gate checks every doc, so a spec can block a build push

- **Spec**: `CLAUDE.md` standing rules; `tools/fc.sh docs`
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: The full gate (`check_project.ps1`, and `flush.sh`) runs `tools/fc.sh docs --all`. A spec or shared doc that fails the lint blocks the build session's push to `develop`, and under the split the build session may not fix it.
- **Recommendation**: The design session runs `tools/fc.sh docs` before each commit; if a doc still breaks the gate, the build session files a feedback item and waits, rather than editing.

### FB-04: U1 is three builds, and the pool layer should wrap the typed fields

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md`
- **Kind**: cost
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Derived values live in three places today: `rpgkit_rules/src/derived.rs` (a rating evaluator: formula, constants, min, max, status modifiers; no bands or current value), hard-coded methods in `stats.rs:258-282` (HP, initiative speed, armour rating, crit, resist), and unit meters in `rpgkit_battle/src/meter.rs` (bands, decay, battle-only). Poise is a fourth (`poise.rs`, max from a derived row, refill hard-coded); AP is `Unit.ap` and `max_ap`, read in about 20 files including the AI and planner; HP is `unit.hp`. So U1 is three builds: the derived class and pools (L, about 8-12 files), the damage pipeline (M), and the stat re-wiring (M). Saves are unaffected while pools are battle-only, which "full each fight" implies.
- **Recommendation**: State that HP, AP and poise keep their typed fields, with the pool layer as a facade over them; only new pools use the generic store. Moving them into a generic map touches every AI and planner file for no gameplay gain.

### FB-05: The pipeline has a third rounding path, and some factors do not fit a stage

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md`, modular damage
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Besides the two rounding points (attack power, final hit; `damage.rs:130`, `:221`), `unit.rs:1091` `take_damage` rounds flat hazard damage, arena pushes and trigger moves separately, applying guard only. Also: `power_scale` (tier) is a multiplier inside the base stage, against "flat modifiers only in base"; authored `power` and fixed-stat units return early and bypass everything; the ally intercept (`command.rs:775-830`) calls the formula twice and splits damage with another rounding. Poise stagger (`poise.rs:164`) is purely multiplicative with one rounding, a floor of 0 and no armour or crit, so it fits only if the stage names are generic. An exact port is possible if multiplication keeps today's f64 order; `rules_golden` will catch any off-by-one at a half.
- **Recommendation**: Decide whether flat hazard damage and intercepts run the pipeline; allow multipliers in the base stage (tier) while flat adds stay base-only; keep the fixed-stat and authored-power overrides; make the first build slice an exact port with every golden byte-identical before any new modifier.

### FB-06: There is no guard status today

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md` (two mitigation layers); decision "What Stand is"
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Guard is a bare `Unit.guard` number set by Defend commands (`command.rs:585`), the resolver and triggers, cleared on a poise break and at round end, and read in eight or more places (log, portrait, session snapshot, poise, AI, planner, metrics). Cover comes from terrain. The two-layer shape already exists (guard plus cover capped at 0.9, armour with K 50); fortify and expose are statuses inside the armour rating.
- **Recommendation**: Keep `Unit.guard` as the situational layer's accumulator, with new sources feeding it, rather than turning guard into a status; or, if it must be a status, size that as its own slice. Treat the cap move from 0.9 to about 0.75 as a balance change with a named re-record, separate from the refactor.

### FB-07: The intended changes move all three goldens; the speed split reaches the world crate

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md`, stats to values
- **Kind**: cost
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Crit from PERC (`stats.rs:276`, `damage.rs:10-13`), potency from KNOW against resist (`status.rs:210`, chance = potency - resist; one changed chance shifts later draws on the RNG stream), and the cap move each re-record `rules_golden`, the timeline golden and `sim_golden`. `Unit.speed` is both initiative and move rate and is read in `plan.rs`, `command.rs`, `unit.rs`, `rpgkit_data` unit rows (fixed-stat rows carry `speed`), the host's UI JSON, the sim print in `sim_golden`, and `rpgkit_world/src/battle.rs:151`, which writes it. ### FB-08: Composure already exists, and there is no corruption pool

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md`, composure acceptance test
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Composure is already a rating row in `derived_stats.json` (`KNOW x 2 + CONS`, 0 to 100, shown on the party, dojo and battle screens). No corruption pool exists in code or data. For composure to run as data alone, these are missing today: a pool mode with a current value and a per-fight refill; a formula max (unit meters have fixed min, max and start); bands in percent of max (bands use absolute values); a distance filter on the `ally_downed` trigger ("within 2"). The pool-change effect exists as `meter` and `meter_set`, with its delta clamped to -10..10 (`meter.rs:285`).
- **Recommendation**: Drop the corruption clause from the acceptance test or give it a task; state composure's max (the formula, or 100); add percent bands and the distance filter to U1's build scope, as the acceptance test depends on them. Is the -10..10 delta clamp the intended limit for pool changes?

### FB-09: Tier as a formula input needs a number

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, tiers; `U1_STATS.md`

Adding `tier` is one branch, size S, but tier is a string (`unit.rs:174`: hero, minion, standard, elite, boss), so it needs a numeric mapping, plus the content check's allowlist.

### FB-10: One share vector cannot reproduce today's classes; two can

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, C1 and C2
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Checked by script over all 7 classes at levels 1-10. Base shares (base / 62) reproduce every class at level 1. One share vector for the whole curve (budget 62 + 5 per level) differs from today's stats at levels 2-10 for all 7 classes; for example a level 2 warrior gets KNOW 11 and DEX 8 where today it has 10 and 7, as its growth puts nothing in KNOW or DEX. Base shares plus growth shares (growth / 5), with largest-remainder rounding on the running total, reproduce every class at every level exactly, so `rules_golden` holds.
- **Recommendation**: Two vectors per class: identity at level 1, and growth identity. A single vector changes 5 of 7 class curves visibly and moves every class-level golden row. Ties in largest-remainder break by largest fraction, then stat order, as `auto_spend` does.

### FB-11: Tiers scale only HP and power today, and budget scaling cannot replace power_scale

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, C7 tiers
- **Kind**: cost
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: `stats::tier_scales` (`stats.rs:35`) gives HP, power and an AI skill cap: minion 0.4 / 0.6 / 2, standard 0.7 / 0.8 / 0, hero 1 / 1 / 0, elite 1.25 / 1.0 / 0, boss 1.5 / 1.1 / 0. HP multiplies max HP (`unit.rs:407`), power multiplies attack power (`damage.rs:115`). Scaling the budget instead moves every stat together (HP, damage, armour, crit, initiative, resist), and boss power 1.1 or elite HP 1.25 have no budget equivalent. A minion budget of about 25 breaks the "every stat 6 to 18" rule. "Tier" also means the AI skill cap, XP `kill_weight`, morale, portrait tier, gear tiers and skill ranks. This is the costliest U2 slice (L): it moves `rules_golden` (28 class-by-tier rows and the non-hero units), the timeline, sim, PHASEFOLD and `checks_golden` HP lines.
- **Recommendation**: Name what replaces `power_scale` (a tier modifier through the pipeline is the natural fit with U1); apply the 6-18 check to the class row, not the tier-scaled unit; keep the AI cap; rename the other meanings of "tier" in code; build this slice after U1's derived formulas exist, so the HP base's tier term goes in once.

### FB-12: Static templates exist already as derived units; the builders are what fail the acceptance test

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, unit types and acceptance test
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: All 47 units except `training_dummy` are already class, level and tier derived, and 38 world characters point at them through `base_unit`, so they read as static templates at a fixed level; no unit row needs rewriting. "Template plus overrides" also exists: `base_unit`, the character's `tuning` (5 keys, used by 1 of 38), `named_items` and passives. What fails "any unit fights with no unit-specific code" today: heroes build through `progression::build_as`, NPCs through `build_unit_in` plus `customize` plus `apply_character`; `apply_character` patches HP, power, armour, speed and AP after the build; the AI profile comes from the base row for heroes and from the entry for NPCs; the sim and Dojo call `build_unit` directly. Only `training_dummy` uses the classless fixed path, with a fallback to warrior stats (KITIDS1 removes the fallback).
- **Recommendation**: Define a static unit as derived with a fixed level and budget, reuse `base_unit`, `tuning` and named items as the overrides rather than a second override system, retire or migrate the fixed-stat mode, and route every builder through one function.

### FB-13: World stage needs a source in worlds with no campaign, and XP must follow it

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, mob growth by world stage
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Nothing passes world state into enemy creation today. The smallest seam is a `stage` on `WorldRoster`, computed by the battle screen from game state (act, or flags), applied when the roster builds each entry; `build_unit_in` needs no new parameter, and the host and sim pass 0. But `roster()` computes a foe's level and XP weight without game state, so XP would disagree with the level fought unless the stage reaches it too. A world with no campaign has act 0. No save change, as the stage is derived.
- **Recommendation**: Say which flag or act defines the stage where there is no campaign, and that the XP weight follows the stage. Pass only the stage now, leaving WORLDFIGHT1's `begin_world` held.

### FB-14: Proficiency levels exist but mean something else today

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md`, C3
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)

### FB-19: IR21's derivation needs a precedence order and a few rules

- **Spec**: `docs/specs/INTENT2.md` IR21
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: Re-run over all 129 skills: exactly the 17 stated differences; after the 7 SWEEP data fixes every skill gets one answer, and the Field bonus changes are exactly the 3 stated (the rule reads `reach_max`). Gaps: engine kinds (MOVE, REST, TARGET, STATUS) are neutral; `hazard` applies to ATTACK only (`ash_cloud_fade` is a DEFEND with a hazard and stays Stand); `tripwire_snare` has a hazard and no shape, so hazard must come before "no shape: Assault"; a short PLUS or BURST (reach_max 1 or less) is undefined (none in data); CASES rows 26, 30 and 31 cannot be derived, as `area` and `target_mode` exist only on ATTACK and SUPPORT. Items have no `kind` or `target_mode`, so they need their own mapping: heal gives Support and Stand; buff gives Stand; damage with an `area` and `use_reach` above 1 gives Field and Assault; damage alone gives Assault. Today `item_intent` (`round_intent.rs:166`) makes foe-aimed bombs Maneuver. The skill's intent has three diverging copies (`round_intent::skill_intent`, `skill::intent_id`, the content check's `intent_of`), and `skill::position_by` uses one to find Maneuver, so a derived Maneuver without an authored `round_intent` would not dash. About 15 call sites compare intents for equality and become "row allows"; `deck_errors` would flag a skill in its second row. The pick must carry its row, so the planner knows which version of a dual skill was chosen. No current skill derives the `power` Field bonus.
- **Recommendation**: State the precedence (engine kind, then kind, dash or position, shape, hazard, no shape), the item mapping, and that CASES rows 26, 30 and 31 are out of scope. One derivation function in `rpgkit_rules`, used by all three callers. Keep `power` as a future default and say so.

### FB-25: Fourteen effect types, and items and meter bands use them too

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U4_PASSIVES.md`
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: There are 14 effect types, not 13: `spell_reach` (`check/simple.rs:72`, applied in `unit.rs`, 1-2 tiles, no shipped row uses it). Meter bands reuse the grammar with a 15th pseudo-type, `crit`. Gear items share it through `apply_effects` with 6 types (skill and status potency, spell reach, resist, trigger, forced move) and separate `gear_*` accumulators rebuilt on every sync.
- **Recommendation**: Name items and meter bands as consumers of the same grant kinds; say where `spell_reach` goes (U1 moved reach to the skill, so retire it, or make it a modifier).

### FB-26: Not every effect is additive; the modifier kind needs combine rules, and meter fits no kind

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U4_PASSIVES.md`, the four grant kinds; `U1_STATS.md`, the pipeline
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: `foresight` takes the largest range (capped) with a first-source id; `unlock` takes the largest level (0-2) and ends in a path refresh; `resist` sums per status and caps at 100; `forced_move` sums bonus tiles (0-2 a row) and ORs two immunity flags; `stagger_taken` multiplies, filtered by action length; `skill_potency` adds (1 + sum), so it pools before multiplying. `meter` spawns a gauge at battle start, raises its floor and opens the meter's skills: none of the four kinds. These fit cleanly: `stat`, `ap_regen`, `status_potency` and `skill_potency` as `modifier`; `proficiency` as itself; `skill` and `unlock` as `grant_skill`; `trigger` as itself. 55 shipped rows hold 80+ effects; 19 rows have more than one.
- **Recommendation**: Write a combine rule per target (sum, product, max, cap) into the modifier kind; add a fifth kind for `meter` (for example `grant_pool`) or fold it into `grant_skill` with a pool declaration, rather than forcing it into `modifier`.

### FB-48: S1.2 audit: the status class

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/S1_STATUS.md`
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: (1) Guard values: S1 names `guard_common_mult` 0.50 and `guard_multi_round_mult` 0.30, but shipped Defends use mitigation 0.15-0.35 (guard 0.3, shield_wall 0.35, riposte 0.15) and `take_damage` multiplies by (1 - guard), so it is unclear whether these are damage multipliers or mitigation fractions; and the closed decision says the common guard is lower than the multi-round one, the reverse of 0.5 against 0.3. (2) "Wind-up start through block 6" cannot be a plain status: statuses are unit-wide and tick only at `roll_over` (`status.rs:290`); block timing exists only in `HeldGuard {mitigation, last_block}` (`trigger.rs:200-210`, `:324-333`), which already means "from block N to last_block, ends on a break or round end". Under 1C guard covers far more blocks than a Defend's own span today, so outcomes move broadly. A break must remove the status instance, not only set `guard_broken`. The AI picks Defend by skill kind and never reads `Unit.guard`, so it needs to see an active guard to avoid redundant Defends. (3) The 17 statuses are a Rust const (`status.rs:47-65`), not data; no `statuses.json`; about 25 call sites use `cap_of`, `stacking_of`, `display_name` and `row_of` without a catalog. `BLEED_PCT`, `DEBT_STAGGER`, `DEBT_STUN` are LOCKED, `COUNTER_MULT` a const, so S1's tunables must become ruleset numbers. (4) Behaviour that differs from the spec: stealth hides a unit only if it moved this round (`round_intent.rs:392-394`), not "untargetable, breaks on attack or damage"; bleed ticks at round end only (`resolver.rs:315`), not "on move or action". (5) Resist is already one formula, `potency - (INT x 2.5 + resist_for)` (`status.rs:210-213`); the trigger `resist` effect writes `status_resist` directly (`trigger.rs:726-732`), bypassing U4's combine; `resistable` is read only by the content checks, and `try_inflict` ignores it. (6) Fit to the six primitives: modifiers (weaken, empower, fortify, expose, haste, slow), ticks (poison, burn, regen, bleed), block locks (stagger, stun), reactive (riposte), rule flag (steadfast) fit; root (locks Move and stops the chase, not blocks), stealth, taunt's authoring rules and guard need special cases. Goldens: guard and 1C move the timeline and sim goldens and the rules contract; `rules_golden` holds if `Unit.guard` stays as the accumulator.
- **Recommendation**: Restate guard values as mitigation fractions per skill, and fix which guard is lower; build guard on the HeldGuard mechanism with `Unit.guard` kept, not a second mechanism; load the 17 rows as a frozen kit table behind the same function signatures first; narrow stealth and bleed to today's behaviour or schedule each change as a named golden move; route the trigger `resist` effect through U4's combine; honour `resistable` or drop it; do the KNOW potency term in U1's KNOW commit. Slices: (a) the table, M, neutral; (b) id literals to primitive reads, M, neutral (AI heuristics stay on ids); (c) tunables to ruleset numbers and `resistable`, S, rules contract only; (d) guard as a status with 1C, L, moves timeline and sim; (e) KNOW term, stealth and bleed, S each, moving goldens.

### FB-49: S2.2 audit: poise pips

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/S2_POISE.md`
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: (1) S2 makes a poise break queue `stagger` for next round; today a break only cancels the unit's unlanded actions, drops its guard and holds poise at 0 until refill (`poise.rs:453-488`); `stagger` is queued only by AP debt. A broken unit would lose the rest of the round and blocks 1-4 of the next: the largest balance lever in either spec, and it stacks with the 0.5 `repeat` multiplier. (2) S2 covers only the hit-to-pips step; rules built on today's continuous bar need a pip meaning: `windup_poise` above max (`poise.rs:305-327`), `unbreakable` holding at 1 or more (`:392`), break chance from taken over before (`:219`), `sure_break` (`:394`), Rest restoring poise (`:331`, `rest_poise_per_block` 5), `stagger_taken` passives, the arena `stagger` key, the trigger `stagger` effect and collision stagger. (3) With shipped stagger 4-20 (76 of 129 skills at 0) and max poise 24-90, a tank at 60 has T 12, so hits of 4-10 deal no pips; 7 skills at stagger 4-5 never matter above max poise 25 unless doubled; boss breaks likely fall (T 15-18); the timeline golden's 25 break lines will not survive. S2 says `roundi(max / 5)`, READY says `Max_Poise / 5`. (4) Pips need a state field beside `value` (the pool view is read-only); U1 adding STR to max poise changes T and every poise, so it lands separately. (5) The battle view already draws 5 pips from value over max (`marks.rs:822-836`) and forecasts from `poise::forecast_hits`; the forecast needs pip fields or the "after" is wrong.
- **Recommendation**: Confirm the break-queues-stagger rule, and ship it as its own slice. Add a decision list for (2) to S2; defaults: `windup_poise` as bonus pips, break chance from pips lost over pips before, Rest restores 1 pip per N blocks, `unbreakable` holds at 1 pip. State one formula for T. Slices: (a) pip numbers and a `pips` field, unused, S, rules contract only; (b) the floor(D / T) rule on every path behind a bar-or-pips switch, default bar, M, neutral; (c) flip timeline to pips with the decisions and real pips in the UI, M, moves timeline and sim; (d) break queues stagger, S, after S1's table, moves timeline and sim.

The frozen kit's 17 terrain rows have no `walkable`, so the loader keeps a missing-key fallback. Terrain hazards (`hazard_status`, `potency`, `magnitude`, `rounds`, `on`) and hazard rows (`status`, `potency`, `magnitude`, `status_rounds`, `damage`) use different keys; unifying renames keys, a re-save of both files and `checks_golden`, after A4.2 defines `EffectSpec`. ### FB-52: I1.2 audit: AI

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/I_AI.md`
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: `ai.rs` reads the 8 status ids in about 25 places, as heuristics, not plain predicates (`debuff_order`, `ai.rs:1087-1125`, has hand-written cases for expose and slow; skill pickers match `grant_status` riposte, fortify, regen). `ROWS` (`ai.rs:1590`) is an 8-name precedence array; there is no Row Z, Maneuver, Field or ring row. The five predicate names exist nowhere, and S1's status rows have no behaviour fields yet (S1.2 unbuilt). The spec maps `modifies_rating(AttackPower)` to fortify, but S1 makes fortify an armour modifier; weaken and empower are the attack ones. A generic "score any rating modifier" would start scoring haste, weaken, empower and burn, which the AI ignores today, moving the sim and timeline goldens. Status ids are also read on AI paths outside `ai.rs` (`plan.rs:493`, `:521`, `round_intent.rs:771`, `command.rs`, `metrics.rs:1331`). The spec's `ai_role` list (tank, striker, skirmisher, ranged, support, caster, boss) differs from the schema enum (AGGRESSOR, SKIRMISHER, SNIPER, SUPPORT), and no role table exists.
- **Recommendation**: Fix the fortify mapping; scope "zero ids" to `ai.rs` or list the other files; reconcile the role names. Slices: (a) predicates replacing the ids one to one, after S1's behaviour fields, M, neutral; (b) a generic scorer behind a ruleset flag, default off, M; (c) Row Z, Maneuver, Field and ring rows, after A3.2, A4.2 and F3, L, named timeline and sim re-record.

### FB-55: A1.2 audit: value, consumables, stance cleanup, budget

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/A1_VALUE.md`
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed (answered in `docs/READY.md` section 4, 2026-11-07)
- **Finding**: (1) Buff items apply at once today (`apply_item` calls `apply_attack_boost(1 + buff_pct)`, `command.rs:688-691`; `buff_stat` is never read). Rerouting them to `empower` through `status::queue` makes them land next round, and `empower` is capped at 25 (`status.rs:62`), so the 50 % Elixir of Focus and 30 % Brimstone Draught would be clipped; `grant_now` (`status.rs:249`) applies at once. (2) Item damage is `w.damage(target, item.damage, true)` (`command.rs:683`): no armour, no guard, no minimum 1; routing it through mitigation is a balance change. Item range and use are duplicated in `dojo.rs:1188` and the AI (`ai.rs:399-429`, `:1809`), and items have no `area` yet. (3) `ITEM_AP` 1 is a constant (`command.rs:1451`); `item_ap` must stay 1 under classic, as classic goldens use pouches. (4) `{flow}` and `{disrupt}` render from the row with no ruleset (`source.rs:652-665`), and classic shares these skills with stances on, so the stance cleanup cannot be a pure data edit; `feint` (1 block, 0.7) is not dominated by Strike (2 blocks). (5) A new budget warning on every ranked skill is a named `checks_golden` re-record.
- **Recommendation**: Items use `grant_now`; decide the magnitude cap or new rows in the balance lane; port item damage exactly first, and make mitigation for items its own flagged slice. Pass a `stances` flag to the token renderer so tokens are empty with stances off. Gate the budget check behind a flag, off by default. Slices: (a) `item_ap` as a ruleset number, classic 1, timeline 0, S; (b) stance tokens and warning, S-M; (c) items through the pipeline, after A2's first slice, rule-gated, M; (d) budget check, flag-gated, S.

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/A3_SHAPES.md`, `A4_EFFECTS.md`; `docs/specs/INTENT2.md` IR9, IR17, IR21
- **Kind**: conflict

(2) A3 says shaped skills always lock to their ground tiles at wind-up; IR17 says an Assault shape centres where the target stands at impact and only Field is tile-fixed. A3 defaults `affects` to enemies for attacks; IR9 says Field defaults to all, as today. (3) A4's step 5 gives a self-centred ARC to Field and Stand and every melee shape to Field and Assault; IR21 gives RING to Stand only and ARC and LINE to Field only, and A4's own counts (Assault 59, Maneuver 14, 19 dual) match IR21; A4 also omits FOCUS (Stand) and DISENGAGE (Maneuver). (4) K1 is nearer L: about 108 `RoundIntent::` sites in `rpgkit_battle` plus the GUI. The schema is a single-line file, so K2, K3 and `affects` edits must go one at a time. (5) `EffectSpec` normalises 5 vocabularies at about 11 call sites; debuffs calling `try_inflict` add RNG draws.
- **Recommendation**: Add RING and ARC beside SWEEP first, keeping SWEEP as a legacy alias under classic until the frozen kit migrates, and remove it last with the `checks_golden` re-record; rewrite A3 section 2 ("Field and drawn rows lock; Assault shapes track") and derive `affects`'s default per row; replace A4 step 5 with IR21's rows plus FOCUS and DISENGAGE. ### FB-220: PR5-19 balance run (durability, dulled, Cold Steel vs marrow)

- **Spec**: READY row PR5-19 ("a balance run ... reported in FEEDBACK"); `docs/sessions/PK2_GRAFTS.md` section 7
- **Kind**: sim
- **Status**: open
- **Finding**: `aegis sim party <L> 200 ruleset=timeline [durability=N] [dulled=lock]` (L 1, 3, 5, 7; 200 seeds), `sim duel 3 10`, `sim feel 2 seeds=200 enc=pk1_channel_duel counts=on [rules=-channel]`. Clear % L1 line / wave / elite / boss: base 46 / 45 / 31 / 8; `durability=` 40, 25, 20, 15 identical to base; 10 nearly (boss 6); 5: 42 / 43 / 27 / 6; 1: 35 / 33 / 19 / 4; 0 (dulled from the start): 18 / 16 / 8 / 1. L5 line / wave / elite: base 29 / 20 / 32, 5: 23 / 17 / 25, 0: 16 / 11 / 18. Duels move within noise. `dulled=lock` equals `power` everywhere (catalog sim allies have no techniques). Channel duel: 32.5% won (median 6 rounds), 2.97 channeled actions, 1.0 Vent and 0.92 crises per fight; `rules=-channel` 0% won (Cold Steel alone cannot win it). Findings: (1) 40 durability is never reached in one fight (the spend per weapon per fight is about 10-15), so a weapon dulls in about 3-4 fights, which only campaign carry-over shows and the sim cannot run; (2) dulled x0.5 more than halves clear rates when it bites early (L1); from L3 the base set is already failing, independent of PK2; (3) lock cannot be balance-tested with sim allies; (4) `FightRes::worn` / `dulled` are recorded, not printed; `feel` does not apply the durability seed.
- **Recommendation**: Design levers: decide the intended pace (3-4 fights to dulled at family 40) before touching the spend costs or family values; consider `DULLED_POWER_MULT` 0.7-0.75 if dulled should be a nuisance, not a lockout; Channel duel still below 40-60 (levers from FB-191 / FB-200: `channel_power` 1.5 gave 45%, 1.75 gave 60%; Vent numbers). Small kit row candidates: print `worn` / `dulled` in sim output, apply `durability=` in `feel`, a sim `mastery=N` so lock can bite (FB-218 (c)).

### FB-68: Squash-landed task branches were never deleted by branch-cleanup: docs delta

- **Spec**: `docs/workflow/cloud.md` "Branch cleanup"; user 2026-11-07 (task branches must be cleaned up after landing)
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@8dbe0cd4)
- **Finding**: `branch-cleanup.yml` deletes a branch when it heads a merged PR or merging it into `develop` changes nothing. A squash-landed branch has no PR, and once `develop` edits a file it touched, the merge re-applies old lines, so it is kept for good. The build session now closes each branch after its squash landing with one commit whose tree is `develop`'s (`git commit-tree "origin/develop^{tree}" -p origin/<branch> -p origin/develop`, pushed to the branch): no history rewritten, `develop` untouched, and the next daily run (after the 6 h age limit) deletes it. Done for this session's branches.
- **Recommendation**: `docs/workflow/cloud.md` "Landing a task on `develop`" step 8 and "Branch cleanup": after the squash landing, close the task branch with that commit; drop the "delete those by name with `also_delete`" workaround for squash-landed branches.

### FB-78: U1.2-S4 (W2-1 switch 4) built neutral; the spec HP formula is held (user 2026-11-07, temporary)

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/U1_STATS.md` feasibility item 6; `U2_CLASS.md` feasibility item 2; FB-09, FB-11
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@8dbe0cd4), follow-up `U2.3-TIERS`
- **Finding**: Built: the per-tier factors are the kit table `rpgkit_rules/src/tiers.json` (hp, power, AI skill cap; values unchanged), read by formulas as `tier_hp` / `tier_power`; `power_scale` became `tier_power` (hits unchanged); `MINION_SKILL_CAP` moved into the table. Held: the spec's `max HP = 60 x tier_hp + stats` roughly doubles minion HP and cuts boss HP by a quarter (goblin brawler 108 to 234, warlord 543 to 392; 32 of 72 wave fights flip), because tier does not change the stat budget: every enemy has its class's full budget at its level. The user chose (2026-11-07) to keep today's `(60 + stats) x tier_hp` for R1, **as a temporary measure**. The user's intent: enemies and static units should have stats so that every unit behaves the same and gets its real HP and damage from its stats by one consistent rule, not hardcoded tier multipliers. Named re-records: `rules_golden` (snapshot keys `hp_scale` / `power_scale` renamed only), `rules_contract_golden` (-1 locked line). Tests: `tier_factors.rs` (5), `tier_checks.rs` (1), `tier_ai_cap.rs` (1), `derived_stats.rs`.
- **Recommendation**: Design: spec per-tier stat budgets (minions fewer stats, bosses more) with the 6-18 per-stat rule restated for them (FB-11: a minion budget near 25 breaks it), then land the HP formula and the budgets together after R1. Docs delta: GAME_BRIEF: tier factors in `tiers.json`, formula inputs `tier_hp` / `tier_power`; HISTORY: "2026-11-07 U1.2-S4: tier factors became the kit table `tiers.json` (values unchanged); `rules_golden` key rename and `rules_contract_golden` (-1 line) re-recorded on purpose; the `60 x tier_hp + stats` HP form held (temporary, user)"; STRUCTURE: `tiers.json` and the three tests. GAME_BRIEF `:249` still names `StatRules.TIERS` / `MINION_SKILL_CAP` (now `tiers.json`, `stats::tier_row`); the kit schema's unit `tier` help says "boss 170% / 120%" but the values are 1.5 / 1.1.

### FB-98: R1-BAL balance options for the timeline fights (50-75 % duels, >= 75 % overall): H6 recommended

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` R1.1-3 `R1-BAL` part (3); FB-75, FB-76, FB-77, FB-89, FB-92; UN-09 band
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@8b046fed), follow-up `R1-BAL`
- **Finding**: Sims on develop @af543321 (`tools/fc.sh sim feel 5 ruleset=timeline seeds=N`, auto driver). Baseline at 10 seeds equals FB-92 exactly (AUDIT-R1b and C02-A do not move the five `tl_` fights); at 40 seeds: windup 10 %, reach 57.5 %, armour 87.5 %, flank 100 %, skirmish 80 %, overall 67 %. Windup is a damage and HP gap against the armour-35 elite `tl_enforcer` (it out-trades the Vanguard and breaks Heavy Cleave in round 3): only its armour or tier moves windup. `know_potency` 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 is inert in all five fights (they use almost no resistable statuses). The stagger and break levers (`stagger_windup_mult`, `stagger_repeat_mult`, `break_chance_*`, `poise_pips`, `max_pip_loss_per_hit`) move reach and skirmish, never windup; `poise_pips` 3 / 8 and `max_pip_loss_per_hit` 2 swing reach and armour too far. `tl_duel_armour` is won by armour-piercing dagger hits, so only the Captain's level moves it. Only windup, reach and armour are duels; flank (2v2) stays near 100 %, and the overall target needs flank and skirmish high. Options at 40 seeds (win %, windup / reach / armour / flank / skirmish / overall): baseline 10 / 57.5 / 87.5 / 100 / 80 / 67; C (`tl_enforcer` armour 20, `tl_captain` level 2, `tl_footman` armour 35, `stagger_windup_mult` 1.25) 50 / 77.5 / 60 / 100 / 75 / 72.5; H5 (data only: `tl_enforcer` armour 15, `tl_captain` level 2, `tl_footman` armour 35, `tl_skirmish` max_rounds 12) 52.5 / 47.5 / 60 / 97.5 / 87.5 / 69; H6 (`tl_enforcer` armour 15, `tl_captain` level 2, `tl_footman` armour 40, `tl_skirmish` max_rounds 12, `stagger_windup_mult` 1.0) 65 / 75 / 65 / 100 / 92.5 / 79.5. Crit shift (FB-75, `sim duel <L> 10`): warrior 81 / 88 % at L5 / L7 (out of the 40-60 bracket before and after), ranger 74 / 56 (L7 down from 66 before PERC -> Crit), rogue 43 / 37, brawler 58 / 54; priest 0-22 % at L3-L7 (pre-existing). `tl_skirmish` seed 7 (FB-77, measured on 98ab973a): ends "fled (round limit)" at round 10 with the party AP-starved (0 or -1) and the enemy Enforcer and Crossbowman alive, not lost on damage; `max_rounds` 12 turns such fights into wins. Hover-card text fit (FB-77): not checked (UI).
- **Recommendation**: (A, recommended) H6: `units.json` `tl_enforcer` armour 35 -> 15, `tl_captain` level 1 -> 2, `tl_footman` armour 25 -> 40; `encounters.json` `tl_skirmish` max_rounds 10 -> 12; `rulesets.json` `timeline` `stagger_windup_mult` 2.0 -> 1.0 (the only ruleset number; it halves the windup stagger bonus, a rule-level change). Reach sits on the 75 % ceiling; `tl_footman` armour is the trim knob. (B) H5, data only (no ruleset number moves): duels in band but overall 69 %. (C) Keep `know_potency` at 0.0 and re-test it on status-heavy fights later. Goldens H6 likely moves (named in the R1-BAL row): `sim_golden`, `phasefold_golden` (both read shipped data), `rules_contract_golden` and `rules_golden` through `stagger_windup_mult`; `timeline_golden` reads the frozen `timeline_kit.json`, so it moves only if the ruleset number reaches that fixture. Warrior's out-of-bracket duel rate and priest's 0-22 % are pre-existing and left for a later class pass. BALANCE_REPORT lines: "2026-11-07 timeline feel on af543321 (40 seeds): 67 % overall (windup 10, reach 57.5, armour 87.5, flank 100, skirmish 80); windup is a damage/HP gap against the armour-35 `tl_enforcer`, `know_potency` inert; recommended H6 gives 65 / 75 / 65 / 100 / 92.5, overall 79.5."

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row 20 (`PurseCaps` "on `game.json` clamped on load"); `docs/sessions/E_ECONOMY.md`; FB-53 ruling; Authority Matrix (schema rule, `docs/decisions/workflow.md`)

- **Finding**: Row 20 is built on `claude/r3w1-20` (all three slices; full gate passed, 2493 tests, every golden byte-identical; review: no code blockers) and held there for this. `PurseCaps { supplies_max, purse_gold_cap }` (kit, `rpgkit_content::source`, defaults 99 / 9,999,999 = today) is read raw from `game.json` beside the data folder (`PurseCaps::beside`, via the engine's `manifest::FILE`). But `game.json` is the engine's manifest: `aegis_content::manifest::Manifest::set` refuses unknown keys and rewrites the file from its fixed `KEYS`, so the caps cannot be set through `aegis content` (a hand edit breaks "never raw JSON", and the next manifest `set` would drop it). The keys are also in neither `kits/rpg/schema.json` nor the engine's key list, against the Authority Matrix schema rule. Today the feature is inert (no cap set, defaults everywhere), so nothing plays differently. Build did not touch the engine (naming purse keys there would put a genre concept in the engine).
- **Recommendation**: (A, recommended) an engine manifest extension point: `game.json` may carry kit-owned extra keys that the engine preserves on `set` and that a kit registers (with types and ranges) for `aegis content manifest` to write and check; the purse caps register through it. (B) Move the caps to a kit-side game file or a schema-registered row (for example a `game` kit table in `kits/rpg/schema.json`), changing the FB-53 ruling. (C) Land row 20 now with the caps inert (defaults only) and fix the writer path in a follow-up row. Build default if unanswered: (C), since W2-4 does not depend on it; the T1.2-S1 and W.2-S1 slices are clean either way.

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row W2-4 (K1b); `docs/specs/INTENT2.md` IR2-IR7, IR10, IR15, IR17, IR19, IR21-IR23; `docs/sessions/A4_EFFECTS.md` section 2; `docs/sessions/A3_SHAPES.md`; FB-106, FB-120
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@c043650c)
- **Finding**: Under rule `field_intent` (on in the shipped timeline; classic and round-intent-only play unchanged): `RoundIntent::Field` (tile target); skills get rows from `intent::allowed` (primary first; the auto order holds primaries only, `deck.order` any row, follow-ups share one row with their opener); the first pick's target picks the row (an enemy -> Assault, a tile -> Field, yourself -> Stand when allowed; `(Assault, tile)` is refused under the rule; `(Support, yourself)` stays for items until K3). Field round: one source tile for all blocks (the planner walks into the band; ARC / CONE need a neighbouring source), each family fills once a round, derived Field bonus (ARC 5 across, LINE 4 long, thrown reach +1, hazards +1 round, capped at 5; constants for now). Shaped Assault row (`PlanStep::area_on`): target-locked at impact (chases 1 tile when out of range at its start, misses if the target left reach, died or hid), `splash_mult` off the target, status on the target only, no hazard, foes only, `+assault_shape_blocks` wind-up capped at the round's blocks. Stand rings are self-anchored and cast only with an enemy in them. New row-only ruleset numbers `splash_mult` 0.5 (0.25..1.00, FB-120) and `assault_shape_blocks` 1 (0..2). Field `power` bonus x1.25 (`skill::FIELD_POWER_MULT`, FB-120) where the derived bonus is `power` (a Field skill with no hazard, not ARC / LINE, reach <= 1; no shipped skill yet). Content check: a dual Field / Assault skill must fit `blocks + recovery_blocks + assault_shape_blocks <= 6` (shipped skills land at 6). Deck orders and the saved-deck check read the derived rows and accept `field`. Data via seed `games/emberwake/data/seeds/w24k1b.json` (aegis content apply): 5 units' deck-order skills moved from `assault` to their derived row list (`founder_hollis` `tripwire_snare`, `tallow_dredger` `scalding_grease_pot`, `founder_elyse` `phosphorus_pot`, `inquisitorial_purifier` `pyre_nozzle_sweep` -> `field`; `calcified_amalgam` `tendril_flail` -> `guard`; appended, so `tallow_dredger`'s `assault` is now `[]` and it falls back to its automatic order). AI: a minimal Field row (a Field round when a source covers `area_threshold` foes, not two rounds running; hidden foes not counted); AI Guard rows open with the Defend skill under the rule; full AI rows are W2-5. UI: the battle menu draws a Field row from what the battle offers; a dual skill has a cell in each row (on an enemy, Assault locks on it and Field aims at its tile; on a tile, Field only); the arrow keys move a Field round's source one tile (refused, round unchanged, if it no longer fits); planned area tiles show in the row's colour (Field marks fixed, Assault on its target, Stand around the hero), hover previews them, the hover card names the row's bonus or the lock / splash / extra block; Field's colour is the theme's `check_on`; the Dojo planner lists Field and locks rows the opener lacks; the party deck order has a Field column on derived rows. Re-recorded (named): `rules_contract_golden` (+2 tunables, +2 promoted); per FB-120 (3) the frozen `timeline_kit.json` timeline row lists `field_intent`, re-recording `timeline_golden` (3 of 15 `tl_skirmish` fights from round 3: the Archer's Field Dressing now derives Support + Stand, so after one heal its Stand fill guards instead of healing again and resting; outcomes unchanged) and `sim_golden` (run 21: rules list, Support / Guard shares swap, +2 guard blocks); phasefold, checks, rules, journey and resave unchanged. No `tl_` deck holds an area skill yet, so the goldens exercise derived rows but no Field round. Balance (`sim feel 5 ruleset=timeline seeds=40`, shipped data, 0 plan failures): windup 65, reach 75, armour 65, flank 100, skirmish 87.5 (was 92.5; 4 capped, 1 lost), overall 78.5 % (H6: 79.5). Tests: `rpgkit_battle/tests/field_rows.rs` (21), `field_intent.rs` (+1), `rpgkit_content/tests/timeline_fields.rs` (+2), `rpgkit_world/tests/deck_rows.rs`, GUI `battle/tests/field_rows_tests.rs` (6+), Dojo and party tests; `ruleset_switches.rs` replays pre-W2-4 seeds with the five orders set aside.
- **Recommendation**: GAME_BRIEF intents / UI: the paragraph above, condensed. kit README (`kits/rpg/README.md:16`): `RoundIntent::Field`, the row-aware planner, `PlanStep::area_on`, `splash_mult` / `assault_shape_blocks`, `FieldBonus`. PORT_NOTES (`engine/docs/PORT_NOTES.md:38` still says `rpgkit_rules::intent` has no caller until K1b): it is now called by the planner. STRUCTURE: the new test files. HISTORY: "W2-4 slice 6 (A4.2-K1b): Field and shaped Assault rows, row-aware planner and Field UI under `field_intent`; re-recorded on purpose: `rules_contract_golden`; 5 deck orders moved to derived rows (seed `w24k1b`)". Spec question (deviation): the row and A4_EFFECTS say "WASD / source tile" for Field aiming; Build used the arrow keys, because A (Autoplay) and S (Self target) are battle keys; tile clicks still aim Field. Accept arrows, or reassign A / S during a Field round? Also confirm: AI Guard rows open with the Defend skill; an empty Stand ring is not cast; `tallow_dredger`'s empty `assault` list (drop the key instead?). Later cleanup: the GUI's tile ghost order and party deck-order helpers copy kit rules (move into the kit).

### FB-123: `brace` at path level 1 takes a capped warrior enemy's slot; Grakka Ashmaw loses Sunder

- **Spec**: FB-119 (`"brace": 1` on `warrior.skill_path`); `ClassDef::path_steps` / `skill_cap` (enemies take path skills in unlock-level order up to their cap)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@c043650c), follow-up `CLASS-BASICS`
- **Finding**: Built as FB-119 says. Capped warrior-class enemies walk the path in unlock order, so the level-1 `brace` now fills a slot ahead of later skills: `goblin_warlord` (Grakka Ashmaw, warrior level 6) loses `sunder` (level 5), which phasefold showed used 17 times, and the AI never picks `brace` in any of the 72 fights. So every capped warrior enemy is weaker by its last path skill, and gains a guard it does not use. Heroes are not affected the same way (they choose their deck).
- **Recommendation**: (A, recommended) accept until R2-W2b CLASS-BASICS makes `brace` the warrior's 0-slot class basic (it then stops taking a path slot, and Grakka gets Sunder back; re-record then). (B) unlock `brace` at a higher path level now (for example 7), keeping enemy builds as before. (C) grant `brace` only through `extra_skills` (Kaelen) until CLASS-BASICS. Separately, the AI never choosing `brace` may be worth a look in W2-5 (multi-round guard scoring).

### FB-124: W2-4 slice 7a (A1.2-K3) landed: item pipeline and mitigation, empower buffs, item rows and area items, stacks and auto-fill

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row W2-4 (K3); `docs/sessions/A1_VALUE.md`; `docs/specs/INTENT2.md` IR11, IR12, INTENT2-K3; `INTENT2_CASES.md` section 6; FB-55, FB-119, FB-121
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@c043650c), follow-up `R4-CLOSE`
- **Finding**: (1) Exact port: item damage / heal go through `rpgkit_rules::pipeline` (`damage::item_damage`, `item_heal`); unmitigated values identical. (2) New plain ruleset tunables `item_mitigation`, `thrown_miss_spends`, `pouch_stacks` (row-only `on` / `off`, default off; the review rejected a first draft that turned them on for round-intent rows, the FB-107 pattern); seed `games/emberwake/data/seeds/w24k3r.json` sets all three `on` on the shipped timeline row (classic stays off). With mitigation on, an item hit takes the target's guard, cover (a throw is ranged) and armour, minimum 1. Buff items now `grant_now` `empower` at round(buff_pct x 100) for their duration in every ruleset (A1 "Fixed (Locked)"); `attack_boost`, stats and Max HP are no longer touched; the `empower` cap / `magnitude_max` rose 25 -> 50 for every source. IR12: a foe use whose foe is down, out of reach or hidden spends the copy when `thrown_miss_spends` is on (a friend use never spends); the GD5 hidden check no longer depends on that switch; `evaded` fires only for a hidden target. (3) Items derive rows under `field_intent` (`intent::derive_item`: heal Support + Stand, buff Stand, area damage reach > 1 Field + Assault, reach <= 1 Field, other damage Assault); FB-121's `(Support, yourself)` exception is retired under the rule (a self heal plans in Stand; the AI drinks its own heal through a Stand round). Items gain `area` (NONE / PLUS / BURST), `affects` and `max_stack` schema fields (written only when set); checks: an area on a heal or buff item, or `affects` without an area, is an error. Tile command (`PlanStep::use_item_at`); area items play only under `field_intent`: Field row lands on the tile at full power, hits all but the user, reach + 1, always spends; Assault row is target-locked with `splash_mult` and `+assault_shape_blocks`. Seed `w24k3.json`: `pitch_fire_bomb` area PLUS, `con_fire_bomb` area BURST (the FB-119 remainder). (4) Under `pouch_stacks` a pouch holds 3 distinct items each up to min(5, `max_stack`); `UnitState.pouch_packed` (saved only when set; `assign_pouch` defaults it to the limit, `set_packed` 1..limit); `roster::auto_fill` (round-robin, higher target first) runs at the kit's new world fight start `battle::begin_fight` and in `settle_party` after departures, returning "Stash short" lines (new battle result key `stash_short`). The Dojo, the sim `pouch=` argument and the host (tile item step; `items_of` area / rows / field reach / Assault blocks) follow. Re-recorded (named): `rules_contract_golden` (+3 tunables); every other golden byte-identical (no frozen fight throws an item; auto-fill is inert without targets). Tests: `item_pipeline.rs` (13), `item_values.rs` (6), `item_area_field.rs` (3), `pouch_stacks.rs` (7), updated `field_rows.rs`, `skill_menu_tests.rs`, `status_table.rs`, `hooks_schema.rs`.
- **Recommendation**: HISTORY: "W2-4 slice 7a (A1.2-K3): consumables through the item pipeline; item mitigation, IR12 spend and pouch stacks as tunables on in timeline (seed `w24k3r`); buff items grant `empower` (cap 25 -> 50); item rows under `field_intent`; `area` on items (bombs seeded); auto-fill; re-recorded on purpose: `rules_contract_golden`". GAME_BRIEF items paragraph and the `empower` cap 50; kit README: `damage::item_damage` / `item_heal`, `intent::derive_item`, `command::item_area_on`, `gear::pouch_fits`, `roster::auto_fill`, `battle::begin_fight`, `UnitState.pouch_packed`, `PARTY_KEYS` `stash_short`; STRUCTURE: the four new test files; R4-2 can name the save key `pouch_packed`. Left for slice 7b (INTENT2-U UI): party-screen pips and `pouch_packed` controls, single-line skill-menu item cells, Field-item marks, the Results "Stash short" line. Left for W2-5: AI choosing area-item rows; AI `try_item` ignoring mitigation.

### FB-127: W2-5 slice 1 (C09) landed: damage and unit rating reads use status-table predicates; no golden moved

- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@c043650c)
- **Finding**: New `status::raises_rating(id, Rating)` / `lowers_rating(id, Rating)` (`modifies_rating` + `is_buff`) and `Unit::active_magnitude_where` / `has_status_where`. `damage::armor_rating` (fortify / expose), `Unit::move_per_block` (haste / slow), `weaken_factor` and `empower_factor` no longer name status ids; each site selects exactly its old status over every table row, and the arithmetic is unchanged (summed magnitudes with one row each, a flat +1 / -1 move step, factors bit-identical with one row; floors and caps kept). Every golden byte-identical. Test `rpgkit_rules/tests/rating_status_reads.rs` (4: per-row parity, the raise / lower split, the old formulas bit for bit incl. caps, inactive magnitudes ignored). If a later table row adds a second status for the same rating and direction: armour magnitudes add, move stays one step each way, attack factors multiply (in the order statuses were applied). Still a literal: `remove_status("riposte")` in `unit.rs` (~1417), a candidate for a later table read.
- **Recommendation**: GAME_BRIEF / kit README statuses: "kit rules read rating-modifier statuses through `status::raises_rating` / `lowers_rating`; no rule names fortify, expose, haste, slow, weaken or empower". HISTORY: none (no golden). STRUCTURE: none.

BALANCE_REPORT: the feel numbers above. Question (gameplay): a unit stepping toward its attacker dodges a reach-2 swing aimed at its old tile, which costs the reach duel 12.5 points and the planner does not foresee. ### FB-130: I1.2-S3 "Maneuver row": I_AI.md adds one, the INTENT2 matrix and the W2-5 row do not

- **Spec**: `docs/sessions/I_AI.md:18` ("Add `Row Z`, `Maneuver`, `Field`, and `RING` rows"); `docs/specs/INTENT2_MATRIX.md:25` (Maneuver's AI row = "row 4", the existing Skirmisher row); `docs/specs/INTENT2.md:126` (INTENT2-AI: Row Z, ring row, row 2's self target, reckless and taunt rules); READY W2-5 ("`Row Z` / `RING` / `Field` AI rows")
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@c043650c), follow-up `CLASS-BASICS`
- **Finding**: Slice 3 built Row Z (= the Field row) and the ring row, and no separate Maneuver row, following the matrix and the READY row. Consequence today: under `field_intent` the gap-close moves (`lunge`, `pounce`, `charge_in`) derive Maneuver only, and only Skirmishers use row 4, so a non-Skirmisher enemy holding a gap-closer never uses it. I_AI.md's slice line also expects a named `timeline_golden` / `sim_golden` re-record, which did not happen (no frozen `tl_` deck holds a RING or area skill).

### FB-143: R3-CLOSE backend audit: no release blocker; five dormant-feature follow-ups and big-picture notes

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row R3-CLOSE (`audit-build` over `origin/main..origin/develop` @e6450e22, code commit W2-6); rows 20, W2-6; FB-139..142
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@3183eed6), follow-up `R4-CLOSE`, `R3-STAGE-SEED`
- **Finding**: Released as #57 (@8d863f58). No golden or fixture changed in the range, layers are clean, and the schema gains only `units.growth_per_stage` and `world.dialogue_roll_die`. Every W2-6 feature is dormant in shipped data, so none of the follow-ups below can reach a player yet.
  - AUDIT-01 (low): rows without `tier` get two defaults: `stage_level` (`rpgkit_world/src/battle.rs:86`) and `UnitDef` read `hero`, while `roster_at`'s XP weight (`battle.rs:215`) and `WorldRoster::tier` (`battle.rs:118`, morale) read `standard`. Fix: one shared default (`hero`, the schema's).
  - AUDIT-02 (medium, balance): 5 shipped enemies have an explicit `spend`. A stage-raised level adds class growth but no spend points (`rpgkit_rules/src/unit.rs:1251` uses the fixed `e.spend`), while XP and purse weight rise in full. Fix: auto-spend the extra pool, or warn when `growth_per_stage > 0` sits on a row with `spend`.
  - AUDIT-03 (low): a `roll` choice on a dialogue loop can be repicked until it succeeds (T_STORY 1.1 anti-save-scum). Fix: extend `tree_warnings` (`check/dialogue.rs:725`) to unguarded `roll` on loops.
  - AUDIT-04 (low): the whole-folder check (`rpgkit_content/src/store.rs:580`) does not report an unregistered game.json key, which `store::set_manifest` does, so a typo passes `checks` and then blocks the next manifest write.
  - AUDIT-05 (low): `stat_kind` (`check/dialogue.rs:108`) checks derived-stat names against the base catalog, while `member_stat` (`dialogue.rs:185`) evaluates with the world's ruleset and silently reads 0 for an unknown name.
  - Unlogged minor rulings for Design to record: `dialogue_roll_die` schema default is `-1` (inherit from the nearest parent world; effective default 20); in `set_manifest`, `null` removes an extra key and an unregistered key in the file blocks every write; plain `Manifest::set` still keeps unregistered keys (tests only); `PurseCaps::problems` now sees the normalized manifest, so a whole float such as `99.0` is accepted.
  - Big picture: (1) R3 features are code-complete but dormant: no golden exercises stage scaling, rolls or purse caps until data sets them; an asset row seeding `growth_per_stage` on a few campaign enemies and one `roll` dialogue, with a journey that crosses an act, would make the release gate meaningful. (2) The sim (`rpgkit_sim/src/world.rs`, `runner.rs:413`) and host (`rpgkit_host/src/lib.rs:231`) always fight at stage 0; a `--stage N` sim option is needed before E/I balance. (3) Stage is the raw `campaign.act`, while checkpoints default `act` to 1 (`checkpoint.rs:47`): `start_act: 1` scales enemies from the first fight; consider `act - start_act` or state the rule. (4) "Enemy" means `tier != hero`, not `side == enemy`, which is fragile for rivals. (5) `ServiceScreen` is reachable only from the UI Gallery. (6) `apply` recomputes the stage at settle time instead of carrying `WorldFight.stage` in the `Tally`.
- **Recommendation**: queue AUDIT-01..05 as one small kit row in a later wave (AUDIT-02 before any data sets `growth_per_stage`); decide (1)-(3) before W/E/T balance; record the unlogged rulings.

### FB-144: R4-1 U2.3-TIERS slice 1 landed inert; slice 2 needs five rulings and the template values

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row R4-1, FB-78; `docs/sessions/U2_CLASS.md` item 2; `I_AI.md` line 20
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@3183eed6), follow-up `U2.3-TIERS`
- **Finding**: Slice 1 is on `develop`: a kit content kind `unit_templates` (`data/catalog/unit_templates.json`, one row per `ai_role`: `id`, `name`, `role`, `base_shares`, `growth_shares`, `origin`; checked like class share rows incl. 6..18 at level 1; editable through `aegis content upsert unit_templates`). `rpgkit_rules::unit::template_for` picks the row for a derived, non-party unit whose tier is not hero (role: unit `ai_role`, else class's); the class keeps gear, path, basics and loadout; a templated unit's stats are `roundi(stat * tier_hp)` and HP `roundi(60 * tier_hp) + CONS*8 + STR*2`. No rows ship, so every golden is byte-identical (gate: 2673 tests, 0 warnings; change-reviewer clean). Build's choice, not in the spec: a content kind (asset-lane editable) rather than a crate-embedded table like `tiers.json`; no unit-row template override; the "growth curve" read as the template's `growth_shares` on the shared budget slope (62 + 5 per level). Slice 2 (rows shipped) moves `rules_golden`, `sim_golden`, the timeline and PHASEFOLD goldens and the journey (maybe `checks_golden`), with wide divergence: max HP mostly within +-5% (minions -4..+3, standard -13..+9, elite -22..+21, boss -20..+29) but `calcified_amalgam` +202 HP (276 -> 478), and a level-3 minion's DEX 23 -> 9, STR 21 -> 8 (scaled minion stats 2-9).
- **Recommendation**: rule on each before slice 2:
  1. Template values. Proposed (count-weighted average of today's non-hero derived units' class shares per role, base x62 / growth x5, largest remainder; all pass 6..18): AGGRESSOR base STR 13, DEX 9, INT 7, CONS 15, PERC 9, KNOW 9, growth STR 2, DEX 1, CONS 2 (18 units: warrior 7, brawler 6, tl_drill 4, mage 1); SKIRMISHER = rogue (base 9/16/9/8/12/8, growth STR 1, DEX 2, CONS 1, PERC 1); SNIPER base 7/14/11/9/13/8, growth STR 1, DEX 2, CONS 1, PERC 1 (ranger 3, mage 1); SUPPORT = priest (base 6/8/11/12/10/15, growth INT 1, CONS 1, PERC 1, KNOW 2). Alternative: the dominant class per role (warrior, rogue, ranger, priest).
  2. Double offence scaling: attack power already takes `tier_power` (minion 0.6); scaling STR/DEX by `tier_hp` (0.4) as well cuts minion offence twice. Scale non-HP stats by `tier_power`, by `tier_hp`, or not at all?
  3. Low stats: scaled minion stats fall to 2-4, breaking DEX move rate, KNOW unlocks and gear requirements. A floor (1? 6?), or scale only some stats?
  4. Role vs archetype: an AGGRESSOR mage (`calcified_amalgam`) takes brute stats. Add a unit-row `template` override (default "" = by role), or role+archetype rows?
  5. Gear modifiers are not tier-scaled (only base stats): intended? And should "non-hero" mean the tier or the side (a named enemy on the hero tier keeps class stats)?
  - Slice 2 watch: `rpgkit_sim/src/variants.rs:70`, `rpgkit_world/src/progression.rs:112` and any Forge enemy preview still read class shares.
  - Docs delta: STRUCTURE `rpgkit_data/src/` add `unit_template.rs` (`UnitTemplate`, `UNIT_TEMPLATES_KIND`, `UnitTemplate::over`; `Catalog.unit_templates` keyed by role); `rpgkit_content/src/` add `check/unit_template.rs` and `source.rs` reading `unit_templates.json` (`UNIT_TEMPLATES_KIND`), tests `tests/unit_template_checks.rs`; `rpgkit_rules` tests `tests/unit_templates.rs`; `games/emberwake/data/catalog/` add `unit_templates.json` (kind `unit_templates`, absent until slice 2). GAME_BRIEF unit rules: the templated-unit rule above. PORT_NOTES: `unit_templates` is engine-only (no Godot original). STRUCTURE is stale on `tiers.json`: it is embedded in `rpgkit_rules/src/tiers.json`, not `data/catalog`. EFFICIENCY repeat finding: a new numeric `pub const` in `rpgkit_rules/src` must go in `LOCKED` / `PROMOTED` or stay private (BASERULES1 scan). ### FB-145: R4-1 slice 2 landed; user ruling: one tier_mult replaces tier_hp and tier_power; duel bands out of reach

- **Spec**: `docs/READY.md` row R4-1 slice 2, FB-144; user ruling 2026-11-09 given in the Build Session: "the tier scaling should be a single tier_mult instead of tier_hp or tier_power ... roughly 0.4-0.6, 0.8-1.0, 1.25-1.5, 2.0-3.0 in order", numbers left to Build
- **Kind**: sim
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@dc8bf52a), follow-up `R4-CLOSE`
- **Finding**: Slice 2 is on `develop`. FB-144 is built as ruled: the 4 `unit_templates` rows (seed `r41s2`; shares round back to the integer points at levels 1-10), `template: "class"` on `calcified_amalgam` and `inquisitorial_purifier` (the second caster: a mage SNIPER that would take archer shares), stats floored at 6, gear requirements (`Equipment::meets_requirements` / `wield_penalty`; the spec's `gear::unfit_penalty` does not exist) and unlock KNOW on unscaled stats, no double tier factor in attack power (the weapon part takes it, the scaled stat part does not), sim / progression / Forge read through the template. Then the user's ruling replaced FB-144's `tier_power` scaling: `tiers.json` rows are `{id, mult, skill_cap}`, hero 1.0, **minion 0.4, standard 0.825, elite 1.25, boss 2.0** (before: hp 0.4/0.7/1.25/1.5, power 0.6/0.8/1.0/1.1; the FB-144 text's 0.6/1.0/1.15/1.3 never matched the table). Templated units: stats `max(6, roundi(stat * tier_mult))`, HP `roundi(60 * tier_mult) + CONS*8 + STR*2`; other units: HP `(60 + CONS*8 + STR*2) * tier_mult`, attack power base stage `* tier_mult`. Formula input `tier_mult`; `tier_hp` / `tier_power` kept as deprecated aliases (no shipped row uses them). Re-recorded: `rules_golden`, `timeline_golden`, `sim_golden`, `phasefold_golden`; the frozen `timeline_kit.json` gained the 4 template rows (W2-5 precedent). Not moved: `checks_golden`, journey, `rules_contract_golden`, `rng_hash`, store resave. Heroes, party and fixed-stat units are unchanged in every golden. Samples (L1 unless noted, HP / melee): Footman 147 -> 186 / 31; Enforcer (elite) 263 -> 281 / 52; Captain (boss) 315 -> 452 / 105; goblin brawler (minion L3) 108 -> 104 / 21; warrior class L5 boss 501 -> 636 HP, melee 111. Test-assumption fixes, not engine bugs: `emberwake_content/tests/ruleset_switches.rs` replays `r41s2.json`; four `emberwake_gui` battle tests pick a step whose target still stands or wait for the attacker's slide (FX1 4.2).
  - Tuning (sim feel timeline seeds=40, party 5, campaign 5; candidates min/std/elite/boss -> feel total, party line/elite/boss %, campaign clears arms/gate): midpoints 0.5/0.9/1.4/2.5 -> 31.5, 75/75/25, 0/2, 1/2; 0.5/0.85/1.3/2.0 -> 34.5, 75/100/75; 0.4/0.8/1.25/2.0 -> 60.5, 100/100/75, 2/2, 2/2; 0.5/0.825/1.25/2.0 -> 61, 92/92/83, 1/6, 4/6; **picked 0.4/0.825/1.25/2.0 -> 61, 92/92/92, 3/6, 5/6**. Every tier sits at the low end of its range.
  - Out of reach under the ruled ranges: the R2-CLOSE feel bands (76% overall, duels 62.5-65%). `tl_duel_armour` (L1 hero vs boss) is 0% at any boss value >= 2.0, `tl_duel_windup` (vs elite) peaks at 17.5% at 1.25, so feel tops out near 61%. Party elite and boss win rates sit above their 50-75 / 30-50 bands at every value that keeps the campaign winnable. Standard 0.825 sits just below a cliff (the reach duel is 100% at 0.825, 5% at 0.85).
  - The floor of 6 flattens minions at 0.4: most minion stats hit 6, so low-level minions all start at 84 HP in phasefold.
  - Generic sim class foes (`sime_<class>_<tier>`) and rules-golden class rows now play their role's template (a mage foe takes SNIPER shares), since only shipped units carry `template: "class"`.
  - Open builder readings: weapon threshold tiers (`Equipment::tier_met`) read scaled stats; a `derived_stats` formula using a stat and `tier_mult` would scale a templated unit twice (no shipped row does).
- **Recommendation**: Design records the ruling (decision row, GAME_BRIEF, STRUCTURE / PORT_NOTES `tiers.json` rows `{id, mult, skill_cap}`, HISTORY: "`tier_hp` and `tier_power` merged into one `tier_mult` (user 2026-11-09); slice 2's `tier_power` scaling and FB-78's separate `tier_hp` superseded; re-recorded rules, timeline, sim, phasefold goldens"). For R4-CLOSE's balance pass, decide: (1) re-target the elite/boss duel bands, or treat L1 solo-vs-elite/boss as intended losses; (2) the party elite/boss bands; (3) a lower floor for minions, or minion 0.5 for variety; (4) whether weapon threshold tiers read unscaled stats; (5) `template: "class"` on generic sim caster foes. Kit README already carries the slice-2 paragraph.

### FB-147: WEBREL1 feasibility check (READY Section 2 row 7)

- **Spec**: `docs/specs/WEBREL1.md` section 7 (READY Section 2 row 7), audited read-only @4093aed3
- **Kind**: feasibility
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@5fa8cab0), follow-up `WEBREL1-E1a`, `WEBREL1-E1b`, `WEBREL1-E2`, `WEBREL1-G1`, `WEBREL1-P1`
- **Finding**:
  1. **Table check**: only 3 compile blockers between `emberwake_gui` and `wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `aegis_core`, `aegis_save`, `aegis_layout`, `aegis_content`, `rpgkit_rules`, `rpgkit_sim`, `emberwake_rules` and `emberwake_world` already `cargo check` clean on wasm32. Blockers: (a) `arboard 3.7.0` (the only crate in the tree that fails: no `platform::Clipboard`); (b) `aegis_ui/src/shell.rs:1456` `Pixels::new` does not exist on wasm; (c) `shell.rs:1489` `ControlFlow::WaitUntil` takes `web_time::Instant` on wasm (**missing from the table**). With those fixed, `emberwake_gui` type-checks with 0 errors. The real cost is runtime: std stubs compile but `Instant::now` / `SystemTime::now` panic and fs / env / TCP return `Err`. Rows: **file reads** live in engine and kit loaders (see 3; `emberwake_gui` runtime hits only `main.rs:85-88`, `gallery.rs:176`); **user files**: `aegis_save/src/lib.rs:29` confirmed, the table misses a second settings writer at `aegis_ui/src/screen.rs:248,285-287` plus `recordings.rs`, `aegis_host/src/playtest.rs`, `frame_tuner.rs:417-448` (dev); `rpgkit_world/src/save.rs:30` (Godot APPDATA path) has no callers; **clock**: 28 runtime sites in 14 files, including the kit (`rpgkit_world/src/new_game.rs:87` `clock_seed`: a New game without a seed would panic), the game (`emberwake_gui/src/battle/{flow.rs:365-449, playback, talks, draw}`, `dojo.rs`, `portraits.rs`) and `aegis_save/src/lib.rs:140`; `web-time 1.1.0` is already in `Cargo.lock` (via winit); **threads/TCP** confirmed (`bridge.rs:20-26`, `shell/headless.rs`, `aegis_cli/src/scenario.rs`, `aegis_core/src/scratch.rs` test helper): they compile and fail at runtime, so they need `cfg`; **process/env**: `emberwake_gui/src/main.rs:76-81` (`current_dir()?` aborts startup on web) and, **missing from the table**, `shell.rs:1380` `process::exit(0)` (Quit); **window**: `windows-sys` already `cfg(windows)` (OK); **renderer**: `Pixels::new_async` (pixels turns on wgpu `webgl` itself); **audio**: compiles, silent without cpal `wasm-bindgen`; **clipboard**: `aegis_ui/src/edit.rs:650-670` confirmed; **bundle**: the table misses `engine/assets` (1.3 MB, mostly tilesets).
  2. **Versions** (pinned): pixels 0.15.0, winit 0.30.13, wgpu 0.19.4, rodio 0.20.1, cpal 0.15.3 all support the web; **no bump needed, so no golden risk**. winit: `EventLoopExtWebSys::spawn_app` instead of `run_app` (`shell.rs:1814`) plus a canvas attribute; pixels: async init cannot run inside `resumed`, so use `wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local` and return the surface as a user event; rodio 0.20 does not forward cpal's `wasm-bindgen` feature, so add a wasm-only direct `cpal` dep with it. New deps: `wasm-bindgen` 0.2.129 (already locked), `wasm-bindgen-futures`, `web-sys`.
  3. **Read seam**: about 45 runtime read sites in 13 files: `aegis_core/src/assets.rs` (15; layer resolution and `read_dir`), `aegis_ui/src/theme.rs:823-1024` (6), `art.rs:71,208,430,455`, `audio.rs:117,241`, `tuning.rs:31-36` (hot reload, native only), `aegis_content/src/file.rs:21`, `world.rs:199`, `rpgkit_world/src/data.rs:51,70,80`, `rpgkit_content/src/store.rs:348,517,579`, `source.rs:58`. Many are `is_file` / `is_dir` / `read_dir` probes, so the API needs `read`, `read_to_string`, `exists` / `is_file` / `is_dir` and `list_dir`. One API covers all of them; **rules, sim and battle crates have 0 fs sites**. Kit loader code is touched (`rpgkit_world` data and new_game, `rpgkit_content`), which the spec's E1 layer list (engine only) omits.
  4. **Bundle**: raw data 1.1 MB, game assets 22 MB, kit assets 7.9 MB, engine assets 1.3 MB; gzip -9 of data + game + kit assets is 27.6 MB (data 0.10 MB, game assets 20.5 MB, kit assets 7.0 MB; xz -9 with engine assets 28.1 MB; brotli not installed, expected about the same since the 647 PNGs and 10 OGGs are already compressed). wasm: a 1.6 MB measured release build (0.35 MB gzip) is a lower bound (startup bails at `current_dir()?`, so dead code is dropped); estimate 6-12 MB raw, 2-4 MB gzip. First load about 31 MB: ~25 s at 10 Mbit/s, ~5 s at 50 Mbit/s. Deferrable: audio (kit 5.3 MB + game 4.1 MB, silent until E2 anyway, about -30%) and `backgrounds/story` (VN stages, ~1.1-1.3 MB each; 8.9 MB for all backgrounds) as a second lazy bundle.
  5. **Saves**: `aegis_save::write_envelope` (`lib.rs:165-193`) writes tab-indented sorted JSON; the largest state in the journey golden (64 states, 700 steps) is a 2.9 KB envelope. A long campaign should stay under ~50 KB a slot, so 6 slots + settings + locks < 0.5 MB, far below 5 MB even at 2x for UTF-16; saves are text, so no base64. Risk: itch.io serves HTML5 games from the shared `itch.zone` origin, so the quota may be shared, and playtest recordings with JPG shots could overflow it.
  6. **Cost** (builder runs), all slices can keep **0 golden diffs** (on native `web-time` re-exports std and the seam passes straight to `std::fs`, so `checks_golden` and the store resave keep their bytes): **E1 L** (2-3 runs: arboard gate, clock seam across engine + kit + game, read seam, user store with `aegis_save`'s 14 read / 11 write path sites mapped to keys plus `screen.rs` settings, `cfg` for bridge, headless and exit); **E2 M** (1-2 runs; needs `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.129, not installed); **G1 M** (rework `main.rs:76-130` startup; `emberwake_gui` is bin-only, so add a lib/cdylib start or use the bin; smoke tests need Playwright: the container has Chromium at `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium`); **P1 S-M** (no web job in `.github/workflows` yet; install `wasm-bindgen-cli` and `butler` in CI).
- **Recommendation**: order **E1 -> E2 -> G1 -> P1**, with P1's `tools/fc.sh web` moved into G1 so G1 can be tested. **Option A (recommended)**: split E1 into **E1a "compiles"** (arboard target-gate, `aegis_core::clock` re-exporting `web_time` swapped in at the 28 sites, `shell.rs:1456/1489` behind `cfg`; small, and it makes the spec's E1 compile criterion true) and **E1b "runs"** (read seam, user store, `cfg` for TCP and exit). **Option B**: keep E1 whole. Either way: (1) give E1 a runtime acceptance, since a clean compile proves little when the std stubs compile (a lint: no `std::time` / `std::fs` outside the seams in non-test, non-CLI `src`; or a `wasm-bindgen-test`); (2) let E1 span engine, kit and game for the clock and read sites above; (3) ship audio as a later bundle part; (4) consider IndexedDB, or recordings off on web, given the shared `itch.zone` quota.

### FB-148: PR4-1 part 2 (AUDIT-07, `elevel=` through `raise_level`) parked: it moves `sim_golden`

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR4-1 `R3-STAGE-SIM` clause (2); `FB-143` / `FB-146` AUDIT-07
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@5fa8cab0), follow-up `R3-STAGE-SIM`
- **Finding**: routing the sim's `elevel=` raise through `rpgkit_rules::unit::raise_level` changes `sim_golden` run 11 (`party 3 1 comp=warrior,priest enc=world:ash_patrol,world:ash_raiders elevel=+1 pouch=con_heal_potion`), line 10: `world:ash_raiders 100 - 3.0 2.0/2 0.82 1.00` becomes `... 0.81 1.00`. Cause: `ash_raiders` fields `ash_skirmisher`, whose base unit `goblin_skirmisher` has an explicit `spend` (`{DEX: 4, PERC: 2}`), so at +1 level it now gets its extra spend points (the intended AUDIT-07 effect). The row's acceptance says `sim_golden` byte-identical with no `elevel=` change, and names no re-record, so the clause is parked: the plumbing is in (`runner::Def.raise`): a staged copy (`stage=` > 0) already routes its `elevel=` shift through `raise_level`, an unstaged `elevel=` copy does not. The part-2 acceptance test (`elevel=2` on an explicit-`spend` enemy spends the 2 extra levels' points like `raise_level`) was written, confirmed to fail on the parked path, and left out of the landing (review M1: no ignored acceptance test); it returns un-ignored with part 2. Part 1 (`stage=N`) landed with 0 golden diffs.
- **Recommendation**: **Option A (recommended)**: approve re-recording `sim_golden` (run 11 only, one hp ratio `0.82 -> 0.81`) as the intended AUDIT-07 change; Build sets `Def.raise` on `elevel=` copies, un-ignores the test and names the re-record in the commit plus a HISTORY line. **Option B**: keep `elevel=` as a plain level shift (sim-only knob, no spend) and drop AUDIT-07; Build deletes the ignored test. Also confirm one reading (no golden impact): with `stage=` and `elevel=` together, the stage grows the elevel-shifted level and the spend raise runs from the authored level (as built).

### FB-150: PR4-2 AUDIT-08 orphan `loadout_ranks` clause built narrower (literal clause breaks valid saves)

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR4-2 item (1) (AUDIT-08: "`loadout_ranks` entries with no matching loadout entry are dropped")
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@5fa8cab0), follow-up `POST-R4-CLEANUP`
- **Finding**: the literal clause conflicts with a save invariant. `progression::pin_ranks` (`kits/rpg/crates/rpgkit_world/src/progression.rs:243-253`) pins a rank for every active family of the built unit "so the class default loadout (stored empty) is pinned too", and the party screen's ConfirmSkills with `using_default` (`games/emberwake/crates/emberwake_gui/src/party.rs:1184-1202`) clears `loadout_class` / `loadout_extra` and then calls `pin_ranks`. So a valid, game-written save routinely has an empty loadout with ranks for families in no loadout list; dropping them would change valid saves and break the store byte-for-byte resave. Built instead (in the PR4-2 phase A landing): `UnitState::sanitize_loadout` drops only the rank entries the existing rank rules refuse (`loadout_errors`: basic, unknown or unowned family, a rank the family lacks), with a test that an empty loadout plus pinned ranks loads and re-saves unchanged. `change-reviewer` verified the invariant.
- **Recommendation**: **Option A (recommended, as built)**: keep the narrower rule (drop what `loadout_errors` refuses) and reword the clause in the AUDIT-08 record. **Option B**: drop ranks with no loadout entry only when the loadout is non-empty (an explicit loadout); needs a ruling on whether an explicit loadout may keep ranks of unslotted families for later re-slotting. No golden impact either way.

- **Recommendation**: engine/README.md `aegis_core` row (:138): add "`Formula::eval_marked`: eval that tells the input whether a name shares a product with a marked name (PR4-2 tier guard)". GAME_BRIEF stats: "On a templated non-hero, a derived formula never applies `tier_mult` to a stat again." HISTORY: none (0 golden diffs). ### FB-153: skill content check silently skips template validation when a family head fails to fold

- **Spec**: found in the PR4-2 phase B review (`kits/rpg/crates/rpgkit_content/src/check/skill.rs:665`)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@738a366b), follow-up `SKILLCHECK-FOLD`
- **Finding**: `entry_errors` runs `validate_template` only `if let Ok(folded) = fold(...)`; a fold error is dropped, so a skill whose rank rows cannot fold gets no template errors and no fold error either. The PR4-2 re-freeze exposed it: the slim `checks_golden` fixture bases lacked the loader-computed `spell_source`, every family head failed to fold, and the golden silently lost its `{jump}` token errors; on develop `shield_wall` and `mend` were already skipped (`guard_rounds` / `position` fold mismatches). The harness was aligned in PR4-2 and all 16 templated skill bases fold again. Shipped data is unaffected (the loader marks every row), but a hand-authored or seed row with a stray rank key would pass checks it should fail.
- **Recommendation**: **Option A (recommended)**: report the fold error as a content error on the entry (one line), so a row that cannot fold is never silently unchecked; moves `checks_golden` only if a fixture case hits it (name it). **Option B**: leave as is (shipped data always folds). Small kit task either way; not queued by Build.
