- **Recommendation**: STRUCTURE (`.github/workflows` row): "`gate.yml` job `web` (WEBREL1-P1, advisory, PRs into main: web test build, artifact `web-build`, browser smoke); `web.yml` (WEBREL1-P1: manual itch.io deploy with butler, main only)". `docs/workflow/web.md` (already rewritten for build, serve and smoke in `61bfb947`, FB-161): take the sections **CI artifact (release PRs)**, **Deploy to itch.io (`web.yml`)**, **One-time setup by the repo owner** and **What differs in the browser** from the full text below (95 lines, passes the repo's markdown lint as a file; the other sections overlap what Design wrote):

~~~markdown
# Web build (HTML5, itch.io)

The browser build of Emberwake on the Aegis engine (WEBREL1, `docs/specs/WEBREL1.md`): `emberwake_gui` compiled to
WebAssembly, drawn on one 1280 x 720 canvas, its files packed into two bundle parts. It is for playtesting on any device
and for porting checks; debugging stays on the desktop build. The Godot web export this page described until 2026-10-19
is retired (`legacy/`, the `legacy` branch).

## Test build and release build

| Build | Command | Contents | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test (`dev_tools` on) | `tools/fc.sh web test` (the default) | Base game plus the Tools menu (Scene Runner, Combat Arena, Forge viewers, Gear Dojo, UI Gallery) and the page probe the smoke test reads | The CI artifact of every release PR; the itch.io deploy until the user calls the game playable |
| Release (`dev_tools` off) | `tools/fc.sh web release` | Base game only: Tools and dev keys compiled out | The deploy once the user calls the game playable |

`dev_tools` is a cargo feature of `emberwake_gui`, on by default, so the native desktop build does not change.

## Build it (Linux, the cloud, or Git Bash on Windows)

One-time setup:

```bash
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.129 --locked   # must equal the wasm-bindgen in Cargo.lock
```

Then `tools/fc.sh web test` (or `release`). It builds `emberwake_gui` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` into its own
`target-wasm/` (so it never evicts the native build), binds it with `wasm-bindgen`, runs `wasm-opt` when Binaryen is
installed (optional), packs `games/emberwake/web_bundle.json` with `aegis bundle` (part 1: data and art, fetched before
the main menu; part 2: audio, fetched while the game runs) and writes `out/web/` (git-ignored): `index.html`,
`emberwake.js`, `emberwake_bg.wasm`, `bundle.json`, `emberwake_1.pak`, `emberwake_2.pak` and `build.json` (variant and
commit). It prints each file's size raw and gzipped.

## Play it locally

- `tools/fc.sh web serve [port]` serves `out/web/` on `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` (Python's `http.server`). Opening
  `index.html` as a file does not work.
- Launch keys go in the URL query, for example `?screen=runner` (the Scene Runner, test build) or `?screen=arena&seed=3`.
- A downloaded `web-build` artifact: unzip it and serve the folder with `python -m http.server 8000`, then open
  `http://localhost:8000`.
- Other devices on the same Wi-Fi: `python -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0` in the folder and open
  `http://<PC's IPv4 address>:8000` (allow Python through the Windows firewall on private networks).

## Smoke test

`tools/fc.sh web smoke` runs `tools/web/smoke.js` on a test build in `out/web/`: headless Chromium through Playwright
loads the page and, through the page probe, checks the boot (loading bar, both bundle parts, a main menu with no Quit),
the no-WebGL message, the URL query, (a) Tools > Combat Arena `goblin_skirmish` to the results screen, (b) New game to
the first region screen and (c) save, reload, Continue. Every page must run without a console or page error. It needs
Node with Playwright and its Chromium (or `CHROMIUM=<path>`); it is never in the gate.

## CI artifact (release PRs)

The `web (advisory)` job in `.github/workflows/gate.yml` runs on every PR into `main` (the release PR): it installs the
wasm32 target and `wasm-bindgen-cli` 0.2.129 (cached), runs `tools/fc.sh web test`, uploads `out/web/` as the artifact
`web-build` (kept 14 days), then runs the browser smoke (Playwright Chromium installed on the runner). The job is
advisory: it is not in the `gate` job's `needs` and not a required check, and a smoke failure does not fail the job
(read the smoke step's log). After it has been green on two releases the user decides whether `main` requires it
(WEBREL1 section 5). Download the artifact from the PR's checks (the `gate` workflow run > Artifacts).

## Deploy to itch.io (`web.yml`)

`.github/workflows/web.yml` is manual only: **Actions > web > Run workflow**, Branch **main**, variant **test**
(default) or **release**. The Merge & Release thread runs it when the user says "deploy". It:

1. refuses any ref but `main`, and stops before building with "BUTLER_API_KEY not set" when the secret is missing, or
   with an `ITCH_TARGET` message when the variable is missing or not of the form `<user>/<game>:html5`;
2. builds the chosen variant with `tools/fc.sh web <variant>`;
3. installs itch.io's `butler` for linux-amd64 from `https://broth.itch.zone/butler/linux-amd64/<version>/archive/default`,
   pinned to 15.32.0 and checked against its sha256 (to bump: fetch the new version and its sha256 on a GitHub runner,
   since the cloud proxy blocks `broth.itch.zone`, and change `BUTLER_VERSION` and `BUTLER_SHA256` together);
4. pushes `out/web/` with `butler push out/web $ITCH_TARGET --userversion <variant>-<short sha>`.

## One-time setup by the repo owner (itch.io page, secret, variable)

1. On itch.io: **Upload new project**. Kind of project: **HTML**. Leave the upload empty (CI fills it). Embed options:
   viewport **1280 x 720**, tick **Fullscreen button**, leave **SharedArrayBuffer support** off (the build is
   single-threaded). Visibility: **Restricted**, then set a password under **Password protect**. Save; the URL slug (for
   example `tactical-rpg`) is the project name.
2. itch.io **Settings > API keys > Generate new API key**; copy it.
3. GitHub repo **Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions**: **Secrets > New repository secret** `BUTLER_API_KEY` =
   the key; **Variables > New repository variable** `ITCH_TARGET` = `<itch username>/<project slug>:html5`. Nothing of
   either is in the repository.
4. Run the `web` workflow on `main`. After the first upload, tick **This file will be played in the browser** on the
   `html5` file in the project's edit page and save (one time).

## What differs in the browser

| Area | Behaviour in the browser |
| --- | --- |
| Quit | Hidden on the main menu (a page cannot close its own tab) |
| Saves and settings | In the browser's `localStorage` for the page's origin (keys under `aegis/`); clearing site data wipes them. itch.io serves every game from the shared `itch.zone` origin, so the storage quota may be shared |
| Playtest recordings and F12 screenshots | Off on the web |
| Audio | The second bundle part, fetched after the main menu; starts only after the first click or key press (browser autoplay rule) |
| WebGL missing | The game stops and the page shows a short message instead of drawing |
| Touch / mobile | Runs, but the UI is built for mouse and keyboard |
~~~

### FB-164: PR4-7 follow-ups for the first real deploy (butler hash provenance, `wasm-opt` on CI)

- **Spec**: `docs/specs/WEBREL1.md` 5 (PR4-7)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@7284e78d), follow-up `WEBOPT1`
- **Finding**: (1) the butler pin (15.32.0 and its sha256) is copied from the Godot-era `web.yml` (commit `1412c1f2^`), checked there on a GitHub runner; it cannot be re-checked from the cloud container (the proxy blocks `broth.itch.zone`), so if itch.io changed that archive the first real deploy stops at the `sha256sum -c` step with no upload. (2) CI does not install Binaryen, so `wasm-opt` is skipped and the itch.io `.wasm` stays 12.9 MB (3.8 MB gzip); `wasm-opt -Oz` usually trims 10 to 30%.
- **Recommendation**: (1) the user's first `web.yml` run (after setting `BUTLER_API_KEY` and `ITCH_TARGET`) doubles as the check; on a hash failure, Build refreshes `BUTLER_VERSION` / `BUTLER_SHA256` from a runner log. (2) **Option A (recommended)**: a later small platform task adds Binaryen (`apt-get install binaryen`) to the `web` job and `web.yml`; **Option B**: leave it until load time matters.

## FB-165 (answered in READY @7a77a417, moved 2026-11-10)

### FB-165: PR4-9 `WEBOPT1` parked: the `apt` Binaryen (108) breaks the web build

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR4-9 (`FB-164` Option A); branch `claude/optimistic-newton-ewkyqt` @`6df0d0e4` (not landed)
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@7a77a417), follow-up `WEBOPT1`
- **Finding**: built as specified (`binaryen` added to the `apt-get install` of the `web` job in `gate.yml` and of `web.yml`; `tools/fc.sh web` now prints `wasm-opt (<version>): <before> -> <after> bytes`; both workflows parse and pass actionlint + shellcheck). With the `apt` package (Ubuntu's `binaryen 108-1`, the version an `ubuntu-latest` runner would also install) `wasm-opt -O2` shrinks the module 13,518,498 -> 9,788,617 bytes (3.8 -> 3.5 MB gzip), but **the optimised build does not boot**: the smoke fails 25 checks with `RangeError: WebAssembly.Table.grow(): failed to grow table by 4`. Cause (`wasm-dis` before and after): the input has `(table $0 4059 4059 funcref)` and `(table $__wbindgen_externrefs 1024 anyref)` exported as `__wbindgen_externrefs`; after `-O2` the export points at `table $0`, the fixed-size funcref table, so `wasm-bindgen`'s glue grows the wrong table (a Binaryen 108 bug with reference-types modules). The acceptance ("the smoke still passes on the optimised build") cannot be met with the `apt` package. A newer Binaryen release could not be tried from the cloud container (downloading the release binary was refused). `tools/fc.sh` runs `wasm-opt` whenever it is on the PATH, so any machine with an old Binaryen gets a broken web build today too (no machine in the project has one: it was uninstalled here after the test).
- **Recommendation**: **Option A (recommended)**: install a current Binaryen release in both workflows from its GitHub release archive (`WebAssembly/binaryen` `version_12x`, linux x86_64, pinned with a sha256 checked on a runner, like butler), plus a guard in `tools/fc.sh` that skips `wasm-opt` below a minimum version (and says so); Build verifies the smoke on the first release PR. **Option B**: build the web module without reference types (`-C target-feature=-reference-types`, so `wasm-bindgen` uses its JS heap and old `wasm-opt` works); a codegen change that needs the smoke and a size check. **Option C**: drop WEBOPT1 (the `.wasm` stays 3.8 MB gzip) and only add the version guard to `tools/fc.sh`.

## FB-166 (answered in READY @381b8746, moved 2026-11-10)

### FB-166: PR4-9 `WEBOPT1` landed (pinned Binaryen on CI, `wasm-opt` version guard)

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR4-9 (reworked by `FB-165` Option A) (the `PR4-9` squash commit on `develop`, 2026-11-10)
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@381b8746), follow-up `WEBOPT1`
- **Finding**: (1) the `web` job of `gate.yml` and `web.yml` gain the step "Binaryen (wasm-opt)": `binaryen-version_125-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` from the `WebAssembly/binaryen` GitHub release, checked with `sha256sum -c` against `7c3bc16599c8274a04d34a504fe4be2047884f900e0e2da2f6fb9cd667183be4` (the release's own published `.sha256` file, fetched 2026-11-10; the archive itself could not be downloaded in the cloud container, so the first runner run is the real check), extracted into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, its `bin/` added to the PATH; the `apt` `binaryen` is not installed. (2) `tools/fc.sh web` runs `wasm-opt -O2` only from version 125 on (`wasm_opt_min`, the pinned CI release; lower it only after a smoke on that version): an older `wasm-opt` prints `[web] wasm-opt N is older than 125 (it breaks the build, FB-165): skipped`, a missing one `[web] wasm-opt not installed`, a run prints `[web] wasm-opt (<version number>): <before> -> <after> bytes`. Verified here: both workflows pass actionlint 1.7.12 + shellcheck; with the `apt` Binaryen 108 on the PATH the build skipped `wasm-opt` with the message and the smoke passed 40/40 (Binaryen uninstalled again after). Measured earlier with 108 (broken build): 13,518,498 -> 9,788,617 bytes (3.8 -> 3.5 MB gzip), so expect a similar saving from 125. **Observable at the next release PR**: the pinned `wasm-opt` ran, its sizes, and the smoke on the optimised build (if it fails, the job stays advisory and Build reports a new item). Gate 2748 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 0 warnings.
- **Recommendation**: `docs/workflow/web.md` (CI artifact and deploy sections): "Both workflows install a pinned Binaryen release (version_125, sha256-checked; bump `BINARYEN_VERSION` and `BINARYEN_SHA256` together) so `wasm-opt` shrinks the `.wasm`; `tools/fc.sh web` skips a `wasm-opt` older than 125 (Binaryen 108 from `apt` breaks the build)." Build section: "`wasm-opt` is used when Binaryen 125 or newer is on the PATH (Ubuntu's `apt` package is too old)." HISTORY: "2026-11-10 WEBOPT1: `apt` Binaryen 108 tried for `wasm-opt` and dropped (its `-O2` re-points the `__wbindgen_externrefs` export at the fixed funcref table; the build did not boot, FB-165); a pinned current release is used instead." STRUCTURE: none.

Dependencies: PR5-1 `roll_table` (the crisis); PR5-2 is not in R5.

- **Spec questions**:
  1. **What is a Channel round?** PK1 4.3 sets `RoundIntent::Channel`, but an intent persists across rounds (IN2), a change ends intent-bound buffs (IN6, `round_intent.rs:283`), and the target kind, deck order, follow-ups and AI rows are all read per intent. Options: (a) a `channel` flag on the round state, cleared at round start; the first skill's row stays the intent, and entering a Channel round counts as an intent change, so bound buffs end; (b) the intent value itself. **Recommend (a)**: tells show Channel when the flag is set.
  2. **Retire the old Channel path?** Today a ruleset can list `channel` in `intents` (`ruleset.rs:115`) and a skill can set `round_intent: channel` (`check/skill.rs:1008`). No data uses either. **Recommend retiring both** in favour of rule `channel`, with a HISTORY row and one contract re-record.
  3. **Timeline default**: ACTS23 5.1 says "off in timeline until Act 2 data", while PK1 4.1 says "on in timeline, inert". **Recommend PK1's wording**, with `channel` added to the shipped `timeline` row in the PK1 data slice.
  4. **"First pick"**: `Pick::MoveHere` usually comes first. **Recommend "before the first skill or item pick"**, so Move and Rest stay neutral.
  5. **Biological Collapse on enemies**: `ap set 0` does nothing to enemies, which pay no AP and get no `ap` effects (`trigger.rs:743`). **Recommend a 1-round `stun` for units that pay no AP.**
  6. **Graft floors**: floors combine by max, so 4 grafts at +10 give 10, not 40, and the Rock Salt flush (-10, Q-43) needs a per-member offset. **Recommend an additive body-only `meter_floor` grant plus an offset on the unit track.**
  7. **Durability switched on by act**: one campaign world (Q-A2 (a)) keeps one ruleset, so a ruleset flag cannot turn on at Act 2. Options: (a) manifest `durability.from_act` plus kit rule `durability`; instances are created at the act line and on later acquisitions, so Act 1 saves are untouched and VERSION stays; (b) the spec's VERSION bump with a migration. **Recommend (a).**
  8. **`channel_basics`** repeats the meter row's `skills`, which already open with no slot (UM6, `meter.rs:157`). **Recommend the `strain` row's `skills`.**
  9. **PK2 and PK3 have no `.1` yet.** Open items: technique lists, recipe rows, recruit stat ranges, quirks and names, revive when the downed cell is taken, and naming procedural keepsakes (the stash holds ids only). **Recommend PK2 `.1` and PK3 `.1` before slicing them.**
- **Recommendation**:
  - `PR5-3` (kit, M): PK1 hooks 3.1 to 3.6; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-4` (kit, L): rule `channel`, skill field `channel`, eligibility, the marrow version in resolve and cost, the opener and planner rows, the Fill order, deck `marrow` and its limit; `rules_contract_golden` only.
  - `PR5-5` (kit, M): Channel tells and the AI row; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-6` (game, M): GUI opener and greyed rows; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-7` (asset, S-M): the `strain` row, the marrow basic, test passive and enemy, the Dojo preset, and `channel` in `timeline`; phasefold is the canary; then a balance run.
  - `PR5-8` (kit, M-L): unit track and the `mark` settle; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-9` (kit, M): body slots and the additive floor; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-10` (kit, M): recipe service; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-11` (kit, M): bleed-out and revive; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-12` (kit, M): weapon techniques, after PR5-4; 0 diffs.
  - `PR5-13` (kit, L, splittable): weapon instances, then durability; 0 diffs under question 7 (a).
  - `PR5-14` (kit, M-L): recruit generator; `PR5-15` (kit, S-M): procedural keepsakes; both 0 diffs.
  - PR5-3 to PR5-7 can start now; PR5-8 onward wait for PK2 `.1` and PK3 `.1`.

### FB-168: PR5-1 `ROLLTABLE1` landed (`roll_table` trigger effect)

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR5-1; `docs/specs/ACTS23.md` PK1 hook (a) (the `PR5-1` squash commit on `develop`, 2026-11-10)
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@6a1977ec), follow-up `ROLLTABLE1`
- **Finding**: `rpgkit_data::TRIGGER_EFFECTS` gains `roll_table` (`rows` of `{weight, effects}`; `ROLL_TABLE`, `ROLL_ROW_KEYS`, `ROLL_WEIGHT = (1, 1000)`). Every trigger path ends in `trigger::run_effects` (skill, passive and item triggers, riders, deferred `ally_hit` effects, meter `rules` crossings), so one branch at its top covers all of them: `trigger::roll_row` draws once from the seeded battle stream (`randi_range(1, total)`) only when a table fires (no draw for no rows or a total of 1) and runs the picked row's effects through `run_effects` with the same event, holder and `rules` depth (each effect keeps its own `to`). Content check `roll_table_errors` (`rpgkit_content/src/check/hooks.rs`): rows a non-empty list; row keys `weight` and `effects` only; `weight` a whole number 1..1000; 1..4 effects, each through `effect_errors` (`meter_set` allowed on meter rules); a nested `roll_table` or `redirect` refused; `to` on the table is an unknown key. Schema help on `skills.triggers` and `unit_meters.rules`. Tests: `rpgkit_battle/tests/roll_table.rs` (5: same seed same row, weights followed, draws only when a table fires, row effects with their own `to`, meter-rule crossing) and `rpgkit_content/tests/roll_table_checks.rs` (4, 19 error cases one error each). Gate 2757 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 0 warnings; 0 golden diffs. Review: change-reviewer clean (3 low, below).

### FB-171: PR5-2 readings beyond the row text and four questions

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR5-2 (@ the `PR5-2` squash commit)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@6a1977ec), follow-up `PHASEFX1`
- **Finding**: Built readings: (1) "the id of a side" is `party` or `enemy` (the battle has two sides; `neutral`, a valid `units.side`, is refused). (2) Heroes, reserved and off-board units are never turned or swapped (as `kill`); the checks also refuse a hero, a protected guest or the `slay` target in `side`. (3) A swapped unit keeps its encounter ref: later effects, triggers, fates, rewards, morale keys and `unkillable` follow the old ref; earlier phase `ai` effects on it still apply on the new base. (4) `swap` hits every placed unit of the ref (as `status` / `ai` / `deck`). (5) "Deck and AI from the next round": unlanded actions are cancelled at a block-start swap; the new deck and profile plan from the next planning (at block 0 the current round's, as the `deck` effect). (6) Trigger limits and facing carry over a swap. (7) Metrics keep start sides, so hits between a turned unit and its old side book as friendly fire (balance still holds; documented on `BattleMetrics`). (8) The static swap side check uses the roster side, even after an earlier `side` turn.
- **Recommendation**: keep (1)-(8) as built. Questions, each with the built default: (a) a unit turned mid-round keeps the actions it already booked, even against its new friends (default: keep; alternative: cancel its unlanded actions as a swap does); (b) accept `neutral` as a `side` target (default: no, two sides); (c) can a hero be turned (default: no, the player controls heroes); (d) node 20 Stage V hostility (PK1 `.1`) reuses `side: hostile_all`, so (a) decides whether a breaching unit's booked actions still land.

- **Finding**: (1) Stage passives are **cumulative** (a member at stage N holds the passives of stages 1..N); the spec says "granted while the member is at that stage", but a battle can add a passive and not remove one, so cumulative is the reading where the battle and the next build agree; the per-stage reading lets data bundle earlier symptoms into a later passive, the cumulative one cannot express per-stage passives. (2) Only members advance on a track; an enemy or guest keeps a `calcify` mark but gets no stage passive and does not turn. (3) `pierce_melee` works only under rule `pierce` (as armour piercing) and on planned attacks and estimates, not riposte or `strike_nearest`; any non-ranged hit counts as melee (adjacent spells too). (4) The breach takes hold at once (the READY row and PK1 2.1), where PK2 section 2 says "from the next round". (5) The skill `unmark` targets allies only (normal SUPPORT targeting), not a turned ally as Quenched Cinder Salt can. (6) The unknown-effect-type message keeps its old list (it is in `checks_golden`), so it does not name `forbid_hands` and `pierce_melee` (the schema help does). (7) A hero calming at the battle end (an `unmark` used, the round not started) settles normally. FB-179 Q4 (graft-only AI Channel rounds) is for PR5-9 (grafts).
- **Recommendation**: keep (1)-(7) as built (each is the built default); for (1) the alternative is a per-track `cumulative` flag; for (5) the alternative lets the skill reach a turned ally like the item.

### FB-191: PR5-7 PK1 balance run: the test hero cannot Channel, the crisis never fires, Channel dominates elites

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR5-7 (balance run on PK1 6.1's watch list); `docs/sessions/PK1_CORRUPTION.md` 6.1; `PR5-22` (longer fights)
- **Kind**: sim
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@ea3bf66f), follow-up `AUDIT-PR5-BUGS`, `PK1-S3-FIX`
- **Finding**: Build `develop` @c1ca8cc6; probes on scratch copies of the data (`data=<dir>`), 40 seeds, `sim feel 2 seeds=40 enc=pk1_channel_duel ruleset=timeline`, control `rules=-channel`; details in `BALANCE_REPORT.md` (2026-11-10 entry). (1) **The test hero never Channels**: `inoculated_hero` has `deck.active: []` and no `deck.marrow`; Strike is a ruleset basic (no marrow version), the warrior's class basic `brace` is a guard (none), and `marrow_lash` / `marrow_bolt` are `channel.only`, so `ai::channel_row` never sees a marrow version. With `tl_hook_thrust` in its `extra_skills`, `deck.active` and `deck.marrow` the AI Channels: 85% won (median 2 rounds) vs 2.5% for Cold Steel. (2) **The AI's Channel choice is a cliff**: with that skill, `channel_ai_edge` 1.0 / 1.2 give 85% and 1.5 / 2.0 give 2.5% (never Channels); `channel_power` 1.0 gives 2.5%, 1.25 gives 85%, 1.5 gives 92.5% (1.25 clears the 1.2 edge only through armour piercing). (3) **The crisis never fires** (0 in 120 fights, although Strain reaches 100 about 1.0 / 1.6 / 3.2 times a battle): `meter::round_end` runs decay before the `round_end` triggers, so a Cold Steel round takes 100 to 90 before the `at_least 100` check; only a Channel round (no decay) ending at 100+ could fire it, and `channel_row` refuses a round whose Strain would reach the max. The crisis table is unexercised. (4) **Vent**: the AI never plans it (0 uses), so "Vent worth it" and "Vent too easy" cannot be measured by the sim; the hero sits in Aberrant Edge (empower +50%) for most of the fight. (5) **Strain's downside is weak** against this enemy: Strain Bite +15 a hit vs decay 10; the only cost is the Edge recoil, 2.6-3.8 HP a fight. (6) **Inoculated dominance**: in short elite fights Channel wins 85% vs 2.5%; at standard tier it is neutral (97.5% vs 100%); its edge is armour piercing and x1.25, not Strain. **Longer fights**: levels and tier change the win rate, not the length (median 2 at levels 2-8); the lever is the encounter's `total_blocks`: 4 blocks elite L2 42.5% / median 3 (control 0% / 4); 3 blocks elite L2 12.5% / 7 (0% / 8); 3 blocks with plate and kite shield, elite L4, 20% / 8 (0% / 10). **Flesh-Tension trap**: no signal (0 poise breaks in the duel; against `tl_enforcer` at 4 blocks Channel 92.5% with 8 breaks vs control 60% with 18; breaks are not split by side). **Feed under Acute Resonance**: never observed (Feed always at 80+ Strain, healing 10-12, i.e. 4%; the -25% applies only at 25-49). **No regressions**: `sim feel 5 seeds=40` 61.0% (identical to R4-CLOSE); `sim party 5` 12 seeds identical to R4-CLOSE; 40 seeds 100 / 93 / 100 / 95 / 80, 0 METRIC FAIL; the `channel` rule is inert for non-holders.
- **Recommendation**: (a) data (recommended, the asset lane): give `inoculated_hero` one marked marrow attack active (`tl_hook_thrust` in `extra_skills`, `deck.active` and `deck.marrow`) and give `pk1_channel_duel` `total_blocks: 3` or 4 so fights last; (b) the crisis: Option A (recommended): run the channel meter's `round_end` triggers before decay (the crisis then fires at 100 as CANON 2.2 says), a kit order change behind the existing rules (golden-safe: no shipped holder outside the test fight); Option B: the trigger reads `at_least 90`; (c) decide whether the edge x power cliff is intended (a smoother AI rule or numbers); (d) Strain's downside and Channel against elites: the levers are Edge's empower, the recoil percent, decay, band thresholds, Vent's HP cost, `channel_power`, `channel_cost` and the crisis table (a tuning pass once the crisis fires); (e) the AI never Vents: a Vent rule for the AI (for example near the max, or before a crisis) if the sim should measure it; (f) tools: `tune=` cannot reach the channel numbers and `counts=on` has no Strain counters (crisis, Vent, time in band, per-side poise breaks); a small sim row would help the next pass.

Under round_intent a Support round may take that member as its target while the unit holds a usable `unmark` skill (`mark::unmark_skills`: known, not used up) or an offered `unmark` item (`mark::unmark_round_target` in `round_intent::target_problem`), and the pick menu on the member lists those rows (`round_intent_plan::menu_rows_on`). **Beyond the row**: under round_intent the consumable `unmark` (Quenched Cinder Salt) could not reach a turned ally before (the Support round-target check refused it), although PK1 3.7 / FB-174 say it may; the same check fixes it. AI: a party-side unit plans its `unmark` skill on the first turned member (battle-start order) it would calm (`mark::would_calm`: by `sync_tracks`' formula the stage after the latest mark goes is no departure stage, so no unmark is spent on an overshoot; not already targeted by another unit's unmark): the first step of the classic draft (`ai::try_unmark`) and a Support round before any tactic under round_intent (`ai::unmark_pick`); deterministic, no draw; it early-returns with no side effect when no shipped skill has `unmark` (all of today's data). Tests: `rpgkit_battle/tests/skill_unmark_turned.rs` (5), `rpgkit_world/tests/unit_tracks.rs` (+1: calmed at Stage V, settles at Stage IV, nothing departs), `rpgkit_host/tests/unmark_turned.rs` (1). Combined gate (with PR5-23) 2923 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 0 warnings; 0 golden diffs. Review: change-reviewer PASS (kit comments named game content: reworded generically at landing).
- **Recommendation**: `combat_hooks.md`: "SKILL-UNMARK-TURNED: a SUPPORT skill's `unmark` (as a consumable's) reaches a battle-start party member now `hostile_all` and calms it at the next round start; under round_intent a Support round may target that member while the unit holds a usable `unmark` skill or item; the party AI uses its `unmark` skill on a turned member it would calm." `kits/rpg/README.md`: done. Questions (built defaults): (a) a SUPPORT skill combining `unmark` with heal, grant or cleanse applies all its parts to the hostile member (as an `unmark` item that also heals does); alternative: only the `unmark` part when the target is not a friend; (b) the classic draft may still strike the member it is calming this round (`rank_targets` over `foes_of`, since PR5-8); alternative: a turned member being calmed is no target; (c) the AI does not walk to an out-of-reach turned member, and uses the skill only, not the Salt. ### FB-201: PR5-27 balance rerun: the AI never Vents (a PR5-26 bug), crises do fire, Vent's numbers need a call

- **Spec**: READY row PR5-27 part (3) and acceptance ("Channel rounds, crises, and Vent in 40-seed `sim feel counts=on`"); PK1 6.1
- **Kind**: sim
- **Status**: open
- **Finding**: Channel rounds: yes (97 in 40 fights). **Crises: yes, but the sim does not show them**: 40 `aegis battle` logs hold 55 crises (1.38 a fight, every fight at least one; Strain 25 -> 65 -> 85 after Feed, Strain Bite makes 100, the crisis resets to 50, decay to 40); the `counts=on` "rounds by band" samples after the PR5-26 `round_end` reset, so Rupture reads 0 (a sim counter gap, PR5-26's). **Vent: never**, a PR5-26 bug: `ai::vent_row` plans `(Support, Myself)`, which `round_intent::target_problem` refuses under `field_intent` (every timeline ruleset; a self skill is a Guard/Stand pick there, as in `self_stand_picks`), so `commit` fails at every Strain 75-99 and the Channel row then refuses a round reaching 100; the kit test passes only because its ruleset lacks `field_intent`. Build is fixing both (PR5-26 follow-up: the Vent pick shape under `field_intent` with a timeline-ruleset test, and a crises counter). With the fix and today's Vent numbers (-20 Strain, 15% HP, a round of Vent plus two Feed blocks: net -10 and no attack), the AI Vents at every 85 and never attacks: 2.9 Vents a fight, 0 crises, 0% won. Watch list (production data, no fix; 40 seeds; Channel vs `rules=-channel`): won 22.5% vs 0%, median 6 vs 8 rounds, Feed 55 uses x 10 HP (4% of 262 cut by Acute Resonance), Strain self-damage from Edge hits 696 HP over 40 fights, 4 of 6 battle wins end at 25 HP or less, 0 breaks taken (Flesh-Tension not exercised: no poise attacker; the 50-74 band is passed within a round). Vent and crises together, on top of the fix (40 battle logs each): Vent -50 / `hp_cost_pct` 10: 1 Vent and 0.93 crises a fight, won 37.5%; -50 / 15: 0.78 crises, 30%; -50 / 5: 0.95, 40%; -45 / 10: 0.93, 35%; -35 / 10 with Bite 10: 0.93, 37.5%; -60 / 10: 0 crises, 7.5% (flips); -35 or -40 alone: 0 crises, 0%; AI Vent threshold 90%: 0.15 Vents, 1.38 crises, 17.5%; 95%: no Vents. `channel_power` (production, no fix): 1.25 22.5%, 1.5 45%, 1.75 60%, 2.0 85%; `channel_ai_edge` 1.0 same as 1.2, 1.5 never Channels (the known cliff).
- **Recommendation**: (a) Vent's numbers (PK1 4.3 item 5 says -20 Strain, 15% HP): Option A (recommended): -50 Strain, `hp_cost_pct` 10 (both mechanics show; 37.5% against this elite); Option B: keep -20 / 15 and change the Vent round's shape (Vent as the opener only, the rest of the round attacks, not Feed padding; a kit row, untested); Option C: AI Vent threshold to 90% (a kit number; Vent rare). The result is knife-edge (-60 flips), so pick deliberately. (b) `channel_power` stays 1.25 until Vent is settled (1.4-1.5 is the lever for ~50% against this elite; a global rule number). (c) A Strain-free hero control (the Bite rider off) would be a fairer baseline than `rules=-channel`. (d) Flesh-Tension needs a poise attacker in the test fight to be measured.

### FB-196: PR5-24 `STORYMUSIC1` landed (story steps and vignettes ask for music; the game's `music_keys` in `game.json`)

- **Spec**: READY Section 1 row PR5-24; ART_UI_STUDIO 3.9 request 3 (the `PR5-24` squash commit on `develop`, 2026-11-10)
- **Kind**: docs-delta
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@859f9d40), follow-up `STORYMUSIC1`
- **Finding**: A vignette's `music` and a new optional `music` on every sequence step kind read the same way (`rpgkit_data` `MusicAsk`, `music_ask`): `""` keeps the music, `none` is silence, a path ending `.ogg` plays as written, any other value is a music key. The content check (`check/story.rs` `music_error`) accepts a key the game lists in `game.json` **`music_keys`** (new optional manifest key, read like the purse caps: `source::MUSIC_KEYS`, in `MANIFEST_KEYS`, `music_keys_problems` refuses a non-list, a non-id or a key twice; `View::music_keys`) or a key whose `audio/music/<key>.ogg` the asset layers hold; an unknown or non-id key is one error, a missing `.ogg` path a warning. Emberwake's `game.json` lists its 9 MUSIC1 contexts and the story keys `story_opening`, `prologue_tension`, `story_escape`, `story_goodbye` (set with `tools/fc.sh content manifest`); the kit names none of them (review M1: an earlier draft held both lists as kit constants). The game resolves a key through its music chain (`music::game_track`: region-scoped file first, then `<key>.ogg`; MUSICVAR1 variants apply); with no track the music goes on. On the story stage a step's music becomes the stage's music when the stage reaches it, before its vignettes (`StoryStage::take_step_music`); an `effects` step's music carries to the next step the stage plays (`rpgkit_world::story::step_music`: the nearest one wins); a vignette's own music still wins while it plays; a `retry` fight does not re-apply it. Tests: `rpgkit_world/tests/story_music.rs` (2), `rpgkit_content/tests/story_checks.rs` (+2: the manifest key, keys or tracks), `emberwake_gui` story test (+1, with `game.json`'s list holding every `music.rs` context). Gate 2931 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored, 0 warnings; 0 golden diffs. Review: change-reviewer PASS (M1 layer: fixed by the manifest key; L1 a tautological test expectation: fixed).
- **Recommendation**: confirm the new `game.json` key. GAME_BRIEF (manifest keys / story music): "`game.json` `music_keys` (optional, STORYMUSIC1): the music keys a vignette's or a sequence step's `music` may name without a track: Emberwake's 9 MUSIC1 contexts and `story_opening`, `prologue_tension`, `story_escape`, `story_goodbye`; set with `aegis content manifest`; without it only a shipped `audio/music/<key>.ogg` counts. A step's music holds from that step on on the story stage (an effects step's from the next step played); a vignette's own music wins while it plays." STRUCTURE: test `kits/rpg/crates/rpgkit_world/tests/story_music.rs`. Art/UI (music README, ART_UI_STUDIO 3.9): story tracks go in `games/emberwake/assets/audio/music/story_opening.ogg` (and the other three), or a region-scoped `<region>_story_opening.ogg` (AI-03 names `assets/music/`, but the player reads `assets/audio/music/`); data wiring sets `music` on the vignette row or the step. `kits/rpg/README.md`: done. Notes (built defaults): loading a save mid-sequence starts from the menu theme plus the current step's own or carried music (music from an earlier visible step is not restored); `music` on `enter` and `end` steps has no audible effect, and on a `fight` step it is the music after the fight; the story keys have no parent context (no track: the music goes on).

### FB-199: Build process error: the PR5-24 landing reverted Design's newer docs (fixed by Design @d2a94371)

- **Spec**: Build landing procedure (cloud)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@859f9d40)
- **Finding**: The PR5-24 squash (`94cc7f86`) was built by applying `git diff origin/develop <task branch> -- engine games kits tools` onto `develop`. The task branch did not hold Design's newer commits (`c8091291`, `3fa8e999`), so that diff reverted their changes under `games/emberwake/docs/` (lore, specs) and `engine/docs/`; Design restored them in `d2a94371`. The same step would have reverted `8e0926b1` and `d2a94371` in this landing; caught before the push (the staged file list showed docs it should not touch). From this landing on, a squash applies only the task's own diff, from the branch's base sync commit to its head (`git diff <base> <head>`), and the staged file list is checked for paths outside the task. Earlier landings this session applied the same pattern while the branch held `develop` (no newer Design commits), so they reverted nothing; PR5-24 is the only one.
- **Recommendation**: known-issues gains the row (this push). Design may want to re-check `games/emberwake/docs/` and `engine/docs/` against its own last commits once (d2a94371 restored what Design found).

### FB-223: PR5-29a question: `rules=` means two things on one binary

- **Spec**: READY row PR5-29a ("`ruleset` -> `rules`"); `engine/README.md` (`aegis battle ... ruleset=<id> rules=<-id,+id>`)
- **Kind**: conflict
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@cf3d93b4), follow-up `PK2-FOLLOWUP`
- **Finding**: Everywhere else `rules` is the rule-adjustment spec and `ruleset` the ruleset id (`aegis battle` / `sim`, host `new {ruleset, rules}`, the GUI's own playback). As the row asked, the launch key `rules=` (scenario files, `scenario shots`, the game's launch args) now means the ruleset id, so `emberwake screen=arena rules=+durability` reads `+durability` as a ruleset id; `shots ... ruleset=timeline rules=+x` fails loudly ("both names given"). No behaviour regressed (the launch had no adjustment key before).
- **Recommendation**: Built as the row says. Options, lowest undo first: (a) keep `ruleset` as the engine launch key (a ruleset is not an RPG word; board and card games have them) and rename only `encounter` -> `scene` (flip the alias table, a small row); (b) keep `rules`; (c) another name (e.g. `rules_id`). Decide before PR5-29b / 29c add more aliases.

### UN-12: CI no longer runs the full gate on develop pushes (user 2026-11-11)

- **For**: design
- **Status**: closed: policy (@cf3d93b4)
- **Note**: GitHub Actions stopped starting jobs at 2026-11-10 23:52 UTC ("recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased"): the private repo used its free-plan 2,000 Actions minutes, about 1,800 of them on `gate.yml` (157 runs in November, a full 12-18 min gate on every `develop` push). The user is making the repo public and asked that `develop` pushes no longer run the full gate (pushes to `main` stay). Done in `.github/workflows/gate.yml`: `on.push.branches` is `[main]` (was `[main, develop]`), plus `workflow_dispatch` for a run on request; PRs into `main` still run it, so the release PR stays the CI check (`gate` required on `main`). Every landing already runs `tools/fc.sh gate` locally first. Release PR #62 (PR5-7..PR5-35) waits on CI; once Actions runs again it merges and the web build deploys.
- **Ask**: record the decision (e.g. "CI on release PRs and main only") in `docs/decisions/workflow.md` and adjust `docs/workflow/cloud.md` (the release section's note that each `develop` push restarted CI) and `docs/workflow/desktop.md` if they describe CI on `develop`.

### FB-250: PR5-43 readings and the Crucible finding

- **Spec**: READY row PR5-43 (1), (3), (5); `PK2_GRAFTS.md` 3; FB-248 (c) (@ the `PR5-43` squash commit)
- **Kind**: suggestion
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@e4505f78), follow-up `ACT1-DATA2`
- **Finding**: Readings built (the specs are silent): (a) "0 Act 1 Strain": a unit without the Strain meter uses a granted `channel.only` skill in Standard rounds as authored and pays nothing, and never becomes a Strain carrier (PK2_GRAFTS 3: a carrier only from the Act 2 graft); a unit that has the meter keeps the normal channel rule for it. (b) The dose record: `dlg_int_dose` stores the founder's id in `sunk_ward.sabina_dose_to` (`sunk_ward.sabina_dose` is a bool), so PR5-44 keys `flag_skills` and `install` on `sabina_dose_to`; one entry per founder (gated on the flag's value) if each founder gets a different skill. (c) `meter_delta` acts on an area-less use only (an area-thrown consumable ignores it, and the content check does not warn yet; the command line prints the unclamped delta before the `[Meter]` line shows the clamped one); it moves the target's meter by the full delta (not capped by the meter's `delta_max`, so -25 stays -25); `skill_block_cost` deltas are limited to -3..3; `armor_piercing` on a non-damage item is an error. (d) **Crucible**: FB-248's "the autoplay has no escape / winch logic" was a misreading: `sim feel world:` already carried `stay_behind` and ran `ai::hold_choice` (the `world.rs` fix only helps `sim party`, `sweep` and `campaign`), so the 10-seed `enc_evt_06` result is unchanged (0 won, 9 lost, 1 fled). The cause, from `aegis battle` seeds 1-10: Inquisitor-Prelate Nemeth kills the winch holder (Kaelen, 242 HP) in round 1 in 10 of 10 seeds (273, or 409 on a crit); with `objective_count` 3 and four founders, one death makes three escapers plus a holder impossible.
- **Recommendation**: (a)-(c) confirm or adjust. (d) Options for PR5-44's Crucible pass: (1) lower Nemeth's round-1 damage or keep him off the winch path; (2) a sturdier default holder (`pick_default`, or a holder with more HP); (3) `objective_count` 2, or a count that drops when a founder falls; (4) deploy the holder away from Nemeth. Recommended: (4), then (2) (data-only, and they keep Nemeth as tuned for human play per the FB-248 (c) ruling not to nerf bosses for autoplay); (1) only if the user wants it. PR5-44 re-sweeps the Crucible either way; until Design picks, PR5-44 records the unchanged result rather than tuning it.

- **Spec**: READY row PR5-51b vs `U3_GEAR_REWORK.md` §1-5
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@19ef84df), follow-up `GEAR-REWORK1-FOLLOWUP`, `CLASSPASS1`, `ACTS23`
- **Finding**: (1) **Row vs spec**: the row's summary lists warrior `flail 1`, rogue `scourge 2`, a `2h_rig` `sprayer`, and keeps `axe` / `mace` among the 1H heavy families; the locked §2-3 matrix has warrior minor `hammer`, rogue third `bow` / minor `fist`, a 1H sprayer nozzle, no `flail`, and retires `axe` / `mace` / `wand`. The row says "per §3.1/§3.2", so the data follows the spec. (2) **Soft penalty not fully retired** (§1): catalog units have no passives field, so the five enemies whose drills live on their `sunk_ward` characters (`calcified_husk`, `guild_master_orlov`, `overseer_grendel`, `mortuary_flagellant`, `proctor_quell`) still wear locked gear when fought from the catalog; dropping the soft-penalty fallback would give them full power (`PROF_GEAR_MULT[0]` = 1.0), so it stays for gear worn while locked and for role-less classes (`tl_*`); the content loadout check does not error on it. (3) **Numbers chosen by Build** (no spec values): `reload`, `fade_step`, `cite_passage` rows (`reload` FOCUS; `fade_step` jump 1; `cite_passage` fortify +3 for 2 rounds, range 0-2), ammo `power_mult` 1.25, `buckler` mitigation 4 / burden 0, `braces` 3 / 1, the four new item names (`hip_quiver`, `fuel_canister`, `ash_cloak`, `forearm_braces`), the keepsake trims (Kaelen's stun resist, Vesper's root resist), wands -> sprayer (a mage's spell sourcing may change), `penal_foundry_apron` -> heavy (mitigation 6 -> 10, burden 2 -> 4). No `off_hand_skill` on `orb`, `shield`, `buckler`, `braces`: spec §4 names Shield Bash, Riposte, Brace and Catalyst Pulse, but `shield_bash` / `riposte` / `brace` already sit in class paths (the duplicate-skill guard) and **Catalyst Pulse has no skill row** (an open spec gap). Also chosen by Build: the `knife` family's reach band 1-2 and the `knife_throw` row (1 block, 1 AP, reach 2-3, knife-only through `weapon_types` + `min_proficiency` 1). (4) `deserters_kettle_helm` and `nemeths_warded_cassock` (named in the row) do not exist in the catalog. (5) **Enemy and preset loadouts the strict rule refuses** (pinned in `emberwake_world/tests/strict_loadouts.rs`; heroes, founders, start parties and class defaults are all legal): `shd_buckler` and `arm_leather` require DEX 10 and a warrior has 9 even with the Prof 1 discount, so these warrior NPCs wear a locked piece: ashlands `mara_voss` (`ember_brigandine`), `hest_the_quartermaster` (`hest_buckler`), `brask_toller` (`brask_buckler`), iron_reaches `orsa_tallow` (`orsa_buckler`), tidewrack `ilse_marrow` (`arm_leather`), catalog `aberrant_test`; Dojo presets no Dojo hero (warrior, ranger) can wear whole: `dual_wield` (daggers; warrior DEX on leather), `duelist` (off-hand dagger), `arcanist` (wand -> sprayer, tome), `titan_deficit` (warhammer STR 22 vs 19; its stat-deficit showcase is now a hard lock, so the piece is skipped). The kit content check does not run `wear_lock`, so `content check` stays clean on these.
- **Recommendation**: (1) confirm the spec matrix (recommended) or correct it. (2) Option A (recommended): a kit row adding unit-level drill passives (or the check resolving a unit's world character), then drop the soft fallback, add a strict loadout content error and retire the `untrained_*` ruleset fields (a contract change); Option B: keep the fallback for catalog-only fights. (3) confirm or give numbers. (4) author those items or drop them from the row. (5) per piece: lower the DEX 10 requirement, retag / swap the gear, or give the NPC a drill (moves goldens: a named re-record); presets: add Dojo heroes for the other classes, a preset class field, or keep them as skipped-piece showcases; and a content check running `wear_lock` on loadouts.

### FB-280 — PR6-3 (`PK3-BLEEDOUT-REVIVE`): Downed Bleed-Out Timer, Occupied-Cell Revive, Act 2 Rules, and `smelling_salts`

- **Spec**: `PK3_ROSTER_LIFECYCLE.md` (§2), `READY.md` (§1 `PR6-3`), `HISTORY.md`
- **Kind**: docs-delta / verification
- **Status**: closed: accepted (@f132eabc)
- **Finding**: Built `PR6-3` (`PK3-BLEEDOUT-REVIVE`) atop `51dd62b2`:
  - **Schema & Content (`kits/rpg/schema.json`, `rpgkit_data`, `rpgkit_content`)**: Added optional `"revive": bool` (`default: false`, `omit_default: true`) on `skills` (`SUPPORT`, non-`SELF`, requires heal formula/`heal_pct`) and `items` (`CONSUMABLE`, requires `heal > 0`, `damage == 0`, `use_reach != 0`).
  - **Kit Battle, Host & World (`rpgkit_battle`, `rpgkit_host`, `rpgkit_world`)**: Added `PartyFate::Dead` (`"dead"`) and `EncounterDef.bleed_out_rounds` (wired from active `RosterRule::bleed_out_rounds` in `rpgkit_world::battle`; defaults to `0` for `Dojo`, `sim`, classic worlds, and `sunk_ward` Acts `0..1`). Deployed party heroes (never guests, never enemies) dropping to `0 HP` when `bleed_out_rounds > 0` enter `bleed_remaining`, decrementing at `round_end` after status/hazard ticks until `0` sets `dead`, logs `"{name} bleeds out."`, and settles `"dead"` (`cause: "bled_out"`). Revive skills/consumables (`revive: true`) revive downed bleeding allies in place or nearest unoccupied non-exit walkable tile within Chebyshev radius `1..=2` sorted `(distance, y, x)` (refusing cleanly with `"Space is blocked"` in planner & execution when none free; preserving remaining round AP less already spent, keeping cancelled prior actions cleared; guarded in `TG4`, supported in classic/item/round-intent AI).

Clicking a downed bleeding ally's party card or unoccupied board token while planning with a living hero targets it for revive without switching selection to the downed unit or being blocked by an occupying token on its tile.
  - **Game Data (`games/emberwake/data/`)**: Applied `seeds/pr6_3_bleedout_revive.json` (2-pass `0`-diff idempotent via `aegis content apply`) + `manifest`: set `rally.revive = true`, added `smelling_salts` (`Brimstone Smelling Salts`, `COMMON` `HEALTH_POTION`, `use_blocks: 1, use_reach: 1, heal: 15, revive: true, value: 15`, `icon_id: "smelling_salts"`), stocked at `sabina_slab` & `varka_trade` gated on `pk2.slab_open == true`, and updated `sunk_ward/world.json` Acts `2..3` (`bleed_out_rounds: 3, downed_won: "wounded", downed_left: "captured", downed_lost: "dead", standing_lost: "wounded", keepsakes_on: ["captured", "dead"]`). Updated `emberwake_world::sunk_ward_roster` Act 2 `downed_left` expectation from `"dead"` to `"captured"`.

- **Status**: open

The six `cohort_*` rows shipped with `temperaments: []` (the check allows it); the assertion is parked as the ignored test `sunk_ward_cohort_templates_draw_from_slotless_temperament_passives` (`emberwake_world/tests/sunk_ward_roster.rs`).
- **Recommendation**: Option A (recommended): name five slotless passives `temper_<x>` with a small stat or resist each, seeded with the pool lists in the table; Build then un-ignores the test. Option B: drop temperaments from cohorts (delete the parked test).

### FB-283: PR6-4 Living Martyr fuse needs numbers, passives and a deploy prompt

- **Spec**: `PK3_ROSTER_LIFECYCLE.md` §3.1, `ROSTER1` §8 (archive), `READY.md` §1 `PR6-4`
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: open
- **Finding**: (a) Tier stacking conflicts: PK3 §3.1 says tiers are cumulative, `ROSTER1` FZ3 says only the highest tier applies; the kit implements PK3 (`FuseDef::passives_at`, `rpgkit_data/src/lib.rs`). (b) The spec gives `max: 6` and tiers `at: 2, 4` but no `per_deploy` or `stasis_days`, no tier passive ids and no `last_passive` ("Calcification V stats"), and no cohort carries a fuse, so no Martyr template is seeded. (c) The kit hooks exist (`roster::fuse_choices`, `fuse_refusal`, `last_stand`, `retire`, `portrait_of`) but `emberwake_gui` has no call site: the battle start does not yet gate on `fuse_refusal` (gating with no UI would block play), and procedural members need `roster::portrait_of` for their portrait.
- **Recommendation**: Confirm cumulative tiers; set `per_deploy: 1`, `stasis_days: 7`; pick tier passives (Option A: reuse `calcify_2`, `calcify_3` and a Stage V passive; Option B: new `martyr_*` passives) and the template that carries the fuse; queue a small UI row for the Retire / Last Stand prompt beside `party_min_refusal`.

### FB-284: PR6-4 crypt count is static; crypt-only refusal text added

- **Spec**: `PK3_ROSTER_LIFECYCLE.md` §3.1, `READY.md` §1 `PR6-4`
- **Kind**: limit-blocker
- **Status**: open
- **Finding**: "`crypts` 0 in Act 1, 2 from the Act 2 facility upgrade or `pk2.slab_open`" has no mechanism (the manifest holds a static int); shipped `crypts: 2` as the READY row states (Martyrs only arrive in Act 2 anyway). A `crypt_only` recruit takes no bunk, so the spec's bunk refusal cannot apply to it; the kit checks crypt places instead with a third text, "Every crypt is taken ({n} of {cap}).".
- **Recommendation**: Option A (recommended): keep static `crypts: 2` and accept the third refusal text. Option B: a kit `crypts_flag` like `bunks_flag` (small schema slice), tied to `PR6-8` facilities.

### FB-315: ENGINE-1 sample game landed; six RPG leaks found in the engine

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-1` (HELLO-GAME1) (@squash `ENGINE-1`)
- **Built**: `games/hello/` on the engine alone (its crate depends on `aegis_*` only, a test holds it): a main menu, a walker sprite stepping over a walled field (arrows or W A S D, a 120 ms slide, bumps on walls and stones), one save slot through `aegis_save`, the engine's `ui_*.wav` sounds through the asset layers, and `scenarios/hello_walk.json` (menu, new walk, steps and bumps, save, menu, continue; under 1 s). Two programs as Emberwake has: the game `hello` and its command line `hello_cli` (`hello_cli scenario run all`, `hello_cli playtest start`, `hello_cli serve`), so the game links no CLI code (the file and clock lints exempt `aegis_cli` on that ground); the gate's `scenarios_all` now runs both games. The agent playtest harness drives it unchanged. Six tests (rules, save round trip and a refused broken save, the command host and its replay, the folder, engine-only dependencies). `hello` became a game id for the layers check, so seven engine test strings "hello" became "salve" (no behaviour change).
- **Leaks found** (engine assumes the RPG; none blocked the sample game, each is a candidate row for ENGINE-2..10, no fix made here):
  1. Scenario `launch.screen` is a closed list `menu`, `arena`, `runner`, and `ruleset` is tied to `arena` (`aegis_cli/src/scenario.rs` launch parse): the RPG's launch screens in the engine's format. A game with another start screen cannot name it.
  2. `aegis scenario shots` takes `screen=menu|arena|runner`, `scene=`, `ruleset=`, `encounter=`; `scenarios.md` calls `link` steps "battle commands".
  3. One CLI per game, each a binary named `aegis`: two games' CLIs cannot both take that name in one workspace, so the sample game's is `hello_cli`. A shared rule (`<id>_cli`, or one `aegis` with a game registry) is a Design call.
  4. No engine helper starts a game: the manifest, the asset layers, the font path, the `Cx` fields and `Options` are assembled by hand in each game (`emberwake_gui` `launch`, `hello_game::launch`, about 40 lines).
  5. `tools/fc.sh` names the games' CLIs (`aegis` for Emberwake, `hello_cli`) in `scenarios_all` and the playtest smoke, instead of reading them from each `game.json`.
  6. The engine's own interface sounds are the only shared audio; the sample game has no music because the engine ships none (fine for now; noted for the asset library).
- **Questions**: (a) the layers check G1 bans any game id as a whole word in engine and kit code, so `hello` (a common word) is now banned there and in the kit asset library check; keep the id as the row names it and accept that, or rename the game to an unusual id? (b) `check_project.ps1` (desktop gate) has no scenario step, so no scenario (Emberwake's or this one) runs on the desktop gate although `fc.sh gate` says it has the same steps; a desktop row or a known-issues note? (found by the review, older than this change)
- **Also**: `aegis_cli/src/agentplay.rs` `kill` no longer leaves `pid` unused on a target that is neither unix nor windows (the web build's warning, reported by main Build; not checkable here without the wasm target).
- **Guess** `[PROVISIONAL]`: the game id is `hello` as the row names it; its sprite (a 16 x 16 lamp-bot, `games/hello/tools/walker_png.py`) is engine-sample art, not Emberwake art, and not for the kit library.
- **Docs delta**: `docs/STRUCTURE.md` games section: "`games/hello/`: the engine's sample game (ENGINE-1), engine crates only; read it first when starting a game". `engine/README.md`: a "Sample game" line pointing at `games/hello/README.md`. `README.md`: the games list gains `hello`. `CLAUDE.md` Layers line: `games/hello/` (the sample game) beside `games/emberwake/`. `HISTORY.md`: "2026-11-18: engine test strings 'hello' renamed 'salve' (the layers check bans game ids; ENGINE-1)".

### FB-317: ENGINE-2 perf step and painter benchmarks landed; first numbers

Scenario step `perf` (`name`, `frames` = 300, `warm` = 60, `budget` {`p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `max_ms`}): verdict `recorded`, `within`, `over` (fails the step) or `no verdict` (load changed, passes); `perf_<name>.json` in the bundle and `perf` in `result.json`. `aegis_ui::perf::bench` and the program `ui_bench` (`tools/fc.sh bench [sizes=] [runs=]`, release build, not in the gate). The sample game's scenario has two budgeted perf steps (p50 50 ms, p95 100 ms, against about 8 to 10 ms measured); Emberwake's screen scenarios record the main menu, the region map and battle planning (no budget).
- **First numbers** (2026-11-18, dev build, no window, 1280x720, cloud): main menu p50 4.6 ms, region map 29.5 ms, battle planning 20.2 ms. Painter, dev build: a whole-canvas fill 3.7 ms at 720p and 8.6 ms at 1080p, 64 panels 5.0 and 12.4 ms, 40 text lines 1.2 and 2.5 ms. The fill alone is a fifth of a 60 fps frame at 1080p in a dev build; a release run is the next measure (`tools/fc.sh bench`).
- **Not built** (AGENTROLES1 section 5, for a later row): frame counters in a real window, `docs/metrics/perf.jsonl` and the 5-record median rule (INTEG1-E3), the start-to-menu and working-set numbers.

Note for PR7-4 part 2: the perf steps draw 70 extra frames before some later shots in `screens_menus` and `screens_hub`; a baseline must be recorded with them in place.

### FB-343: ENGINE-14 golden bisect landed

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-14` (GOLDEN-BISECT1), `FB-334` repeats (@squash `ENGINE-14`)
- **Built**: (1) `aegis_core::switches`: `on("<name>")` is true when the name is in the comma list of the environment variable `AEGIS_SWITCHES`, and only in a debug build (a release build never reads it, so no switch reaches a shipped game); read once per process; tests `aegis_core/tests/switches.rs`. (2) `tools/fc.sh golden-bisect <golden> <switch> [--keep DIR]` (`tools/planner/golden_bisect.py`): finds the golden by test name (`timeline`, `sim`, `rules`, `phasefold`, `journey`, `checks`, `rules_report`, `rng_hash`; any crate test that records under `RECORD=1`), refuses a switch no code reads, records it with the switch off and then on (`RECORD=1`, the committed fixtures restored byte for byte between and after the runs, whatever happens), and prints per fixture what moved by entry label (fight, sim command line, unit, case; else the index), plus what the switch-off run already moves against the committed golden (the branch's own drift). `--keep DIR` keeps both recordings; `golden-bisect list` lists the goldens and every switch the code reads. Tests `tools/planner/test_golden_bisect.py` (3, in the gate's planner tests). Tried end to end with a scratch switch (`+1` on every hit, removed again): timeline 18 of 18 fights moved, sim 17 of 22 runs, in about a minute each warm; fixtures unchanged after.
- **How a builder uses it**: put the golden-moving rule behind `aegis_core::switches::on("regrant")` (the crate depends on `aegis_core`), run `tools/fc.sh golden-bisect timeline regrant`, and report the list. Once the user rules, the switch goes (the rule kept or dropped) and the golden is re-recorded as usual. For main Build: the parked `REGRANT_RULE` and retarget patch fit this as two switches.
- **Docs delta**: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (the `fc.sh` row): "`golden-bisect <golden> <switch>`: a golden recorded with a test-only switch (`aegis_core::switches`) off and on; lists what moves; fixtures restored." `engine/README.md` (aegis_core): "`switches`: named test-only switches (`AEGIS_SWITCHES`, debug builds only)." `HISTORY.md`: none.

### FB-345: ENGINE-15 tools helpers landed

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-15` (TOOLS-HELP1) (@squash `ENGINE-15`)
- **Built**: (1) `tools/fc.sh golden-bisect repro <switch>`: builds the bins, replays every `games/*/playtests/repro/*.json` with the game's CLI (`game.json` `cli`, else `<id>_cli`) with the switch off and then on, and prints per recording whether it still matches, the divergence lines when not, and "N of M recording(s) move"; refuses a switch no code reads, like the golden mode. Tried with a scratch switch (removed again): the one recording diverged only with the switch on. (2) `tools/fc.sh schema-field <table> <field> <json> [--after <key>] [--replace]` (`tools/planner/schema_field.py`): `<table>` is `content.<kind>` or `world.<kind>`, or a bare kind when only one section has it (`items` and `encounters` are in both, so they must be qualified); the json is the field object, its `key` is `<field>`; added last or after `--after`; a duplicate key is refused unless `--replace` (keeps its place); writes the file in its own one-line form (compact, UTF-8, no trailing newline), so the diff is the new field alone, and refuses to rewrite a file not in that form. (3) `tools/fc.sh seed-from <kind> <id> [<world>] [--set k=v]... [--out F [--append]]` (`tools/planner/seed_from.py`): reads the stored entry through the new `aegis content get <kind> <id> [world=<id>]` (`aegis_content::store::get`; prints the entry as one JSON line), applies each `--set` (dotted keys reach inside, a value is JSON when it parses else a string, `k=` removes the key), writes whole floats as whole numbers, and prints the seed `{"steps":[{"op":"upsert",...}]}` or writes it to F (`--append` adds a step). It writes no data; apply with `tools/fc.sh content apply F`. Checked: a seed with no change applied to `classes warrior` leaves `classes.json` byte for byte unchanged (restored after). Tests `tools/planner/test_tools_help.py` (5) and a repro test in `test_golden_bisect.py` (4 there now), in the gate's planner tests.
- **Guess**: `content get` numbers print as the store reads them (`1.0`); the seed helper turns whole floats back into whole numbers rather than changing the CLI's output.
- **Docs delta**: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (the `fc.sh` row): "`golden-bisect repro <switch>`: the repro replays off and on; `schema-field <table> <field> <json>`: a field into `kits/rpg/schema.json` byte for byte; `seed-from <kind> <id> [<world>] --set k=v`: a seed from a stored entry with changes, for `content apply`." `engine/README.md` (aegis_content / aegis_cli): "`content get <kind> <id> [world=]`: one stored entry as a JSON line." `HISTORY.md`: none.

### FB-347: ENGINE-16 tools helpers landed; scenario shots are not reproducible run to run

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-16` (TOOLS-HELP2), `FB-350` repeats (@squash `ENGINE-16`)
- **Built**: (1) `tools/fc.sh scenario shots-all out=<dir> [compare=<before dir> [tolerance=8] [pixels=300]] [size=] [profile=] ...`: runs every scenario of the game (`scenario run all`) into a scratch folder, then copies each shot into `<dir>` as `<scenario>__<shot>.png` (`@<WxH>` added only when a scenario ran at more than one size; golden `.diff.png` images and the `playing/` frame sequences left out) with `index.txt`; on a failed scenario the bundles are kept and named. `compare=` lists the shots changed (most pixels first, with the count), new and gone against an earlier `<dir>`: a pixel changed when a channel moved more than `tolerance`, a shot when more than `pixels` did (`tools/planner/shots_all.py`, plain Python PNG reader, no Pillow). Today: 68 shots of 19 scenarios; a compare of 68 shots about 30 s. (2) `tools/fc.sh rename <old> <new> [<path>...] [--strings] [--comments] [--dry]` (`tools/planner/rename_ident.py`): renames a whole-word identifier in tracked `.rs` and `.json` files (or the paths given). In Rust only code changes: string literals (plain, byte, raw), char literals and comments (line, nested block, doc) are left unless `--strings` / `--comments`, and the hits left are listed per file. In JSON an object key or a string value equal to `<old>` is renamed (`--strings`: also as a word inside longer strings), the file's layout kept. `legacy/`, shipped game data (`games/*/data/`, through `aegis content`) and `tests/fixtures/` (goldens) are never touched, only listed. Tried: `MAX_FRAME_MS` renamed across engine, kit and game, workspace built clean with every target, then reverted. Tests `tools/planner/test_tools_help2.py` (6), in the gate's planner tests.
- **Finding (for main Build and `PR7-4`)**: two runs of the same build give different shots. With tolerance 8, 11 of 68 shots move more than 300 pixels (`tallow_shop` `chandler_talk` 120,884; `story_battle_hub` `t1_battle_beat` 87,144 and `t2_victory_beat` 38,366; the battle-bar shots of `battle_menu_retreat` and `cages_auto_plan` 1,400 to 2,000), and the hub screens of `screens_hub` 100 to 300 (idle animations, by the look of it). That is why `compare` counts pixels instead of bytes and why its default allowance is 300. The screen baselines `PR7-4` waits to record would need an allowance like that, or the shots taken at a fixed animation time. No change made: whether shots should be frame-exact is for Design.
- **Guesses**: `compare` defaults tolerance 8, pixels 300 (above the hub drift seen; battle animations still show); the `playing/` frame sequences are left out of the flat folder.
- **Docs delta**: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (the `fc.sh` row): "`scenario shots-all out=<dir> [compare=<before>]`: every scenario's shots in one folder, with changed, new and gone shots against an earlier folder; `rename <old> <new>`: an identifier across Rust and JSON, strings and comments left unless asked." `HISTORY.md`: none.

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `PR7-42` (PACE1) items 1-4, PT-17, PT-18, PT-19, PT-39 (@squash `PR7-42`)
- **Built**: (1) kit zone-binding keys `visit_cap` (patrols per location visit, all zones counted, reset on entry), `rest_beaten` (a beaten patrol encounter is not picked again until `gs.time` changes) and `repeat_xp_pct` (XP percent per repeat win); a binding with any of them sends nothing before its own `steps_min`. Optional save key `explore.patrols` (`visit`, `won`, `day`), written only when a binding uses the keys, no save version bump. All 7 Sunk Ward locations use steps 40-60, cap 2, rest on, XP [75, 50, 25]. (2) Quest field `rec_level` (kit schema); the board shows "Lv N" and "Recommended level N." and lists rated jobs lowest first, unrated after in file order; The Cages 4, The Sweep 5. (3) Shop `chandler_stall` (the Candle-Maker) sells Warded Tallow for 5 Scrap; world `rest.needs_upkeep` true; `purse::starved_ap` / `upkeep_after` show "1 day, 1 Tallow, -2 AP" on a trip that empties the purse, an "On arrival" line on Travel and a red legend row at 0 Tallow. (4) Fight 2 hint "Use Vesper's smoke: hide, guard each other, drive them off."; exit tile (11, 4) removed. All data through seed `pr7_42`.

- **Questions**: (1) Should the third repeat itself pay 0? (2) Should `rest_beaten` be per zone? The Crossroads slum lane binds one encounter, so it goes quiet for the day after one win. (3) The round planner refuses every exit tile as a move target ("That tile can't be moved to."); that may break flee exits elsewhere; worth a row? (4) The refusal at 0 Tallow is the kit's generic "Not enough upkeep to rest."; name the game's upkeep item instead?

"Quest `rec_level` shows on the board; rated jobs list lowest first (The Cages 4, The Sweep 5)." `kits/rpg/README.md`: `explore.patrols` save key; `battle::settle_xp_pct`, `Tally.xp_pct`, `progression::award_encounter_pct`; `board::rec_level` / `rec_level_text`; `purse::starved_ap` / `upkeep_after`. `HISTORY.md`: "2026-11-19 Fight 2 (Rooftop) exit tile removed and hint reworded (PR7-42 PT-39): a round plan refuses moves onto exit tiles. ### FB-349: ENGINE-17 shot clock landed; every scenario shot byte for byte in two runs

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-17` (SHOT-CLOCK1), `FB-347` (@squash `ENGINE-17`)
- **Built**: (1) `aegis_core::clock::Instant` is now a thin wrapper over the platform instant (same methods and operators, `From` both ways for an API such as winit's `WaitUntil`). `clock::step_on()` switches the process to stepped time, `clock::advance(d)` moves it, `Instant::wall()` / `wall_elapsed()` always read the real clock, and `clock::system_now()` gives the date on the same clock (from 2026-01-01 when stepped). Off, `now()` is the platform's own, so windows and shipped runs are unchanged. (2) `aegis_ui::shell::headless`: launch key `clock=step`. The clock is stepped before the first screen opens, no frame is drawn at the pace, each drawn frame first moves time on one frame step (1 / fps), and `frames` takes `ms` (that much game time) and `since_open_ms` (until the top screen has been open that long). Idle exit, pacing, perf frame times (`perf::ms_since`) and clip limits read wall time. (3) `aegis scenario`: every run with no window passes `clock=step`; start-up, each `wait` look (one frame, `WAIT_FRAMES`) and `pause` ask for frames instead of sleeping; shot step `t` (seconds 0 to 60 after the top screen opened, no window only); authoring page `engine/docs/authoring/scenarios.md` section "The shot clock". (4) Kit: a new game's clock seed reads `clock::system_now()`. That was the last difference: one run dropped Watch Hookbill and the other did not. (5) The agent playtest shares `headless_args` and stays on real time: the scenario runner adds `clock=step` itself. (6) Gate step `shotsexact` (`tools/gate_steps.txt`, after `scenarios`): the scenarios step keeps its shots under `target/fc_shots/<game>/`, then every scenario runs again and each shot must be byte for byte the same (`shots_all.py compare ... strict=1`, tolerance 0, pixels 0). Today it reports 74 Emberwake shots (20 scenarios) and 3 hello shots the same; it adds one scenarios run (about 3.5 minutes) to the gate.
- **Changed outside the engine**: `games/emberwake/scenarios/story_battle_hub.json`: shot `t1_battle_beat` takes `"t": 1.0`. At 0 s the battle's fade-in is still black and the shot is refused as blank. Test files that built `std::time::Instant` for the clock's type now name `aegis_core::clock::Instant` (aegis_ui tests, emberwake_gui battle tests). The bot run's `Headless` sets `stepped: false`.
- **Tests**: `aegis_core/tests/clock_step.rs` (stepped time, wall time, the date); `aegis_ui/tests/headless.rs` (`clock=` parsed, a bad value refused); `aegis_cli/tests/scenario.rs` (`t` parsed and bounded, `clock=step` passed, the start asks for frames, a pause with no window is one `frames` `ms` request); `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p emberwake_gui` clean. Goldens unchanged.
- **Guesses**: `t` means "at least t s after the top screen opened": the clock never runs back, so a shot past that time is taken at once. Default 0 is "as soon as the frames after the last action are drawn". A screen counts as opened when the stack's depth or top id changes. A `wait` draws one frame per look. `shotsexact` is in the gate rather than an occasional check: drift would otherwise come back unseen. Design may move it out if gate time matters more.
- **Docs delta**: `engine/README.md` (aegis_core): "`clock`: the one wall clock; stepped in a run with no window (the shot clock, `step_on` / `advance` / `system_now`), `Instant::wall` for real time." `docs/WORKFLOW.md` (gate steps): "`shotsexact`: every scenario again, each shot byte for byte the same." `HISTORY.md`: "2026-11-19 scenario shots compared with a pixel allowance for idle animation (`FB-347`): replaced by the shot clock (`ENGINE-17`); runs are frame-exact."

### FB-351: ENGINE-18 layout parts for long lists landed; AI-27 can go ahead

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `ENGINE-18` (LAYOUT-KIT2), Art/UI `AI-27` (@squash `ENGINE-18`)
- **Built** (`aegis_ui::screen_layout`, `panes`, `ui`): (1) A `list_row` region shorter than its list becomes a scroll area. Its id is `<screen>.<region>`, the wheel scrolls it, and a scroll bar shows. Every row stays a widget with its action whether it shows or not, so `settings_controls.f_bindings.11` resolves, and a row scrolled out has no room to be clicked by the mouse. When the keys or a pad move the focus (the ring shows), the list scrolls to keep the focused row and one row on each side in view, so arrow down walks the whole list. The new `Ui::scroll_to` writes the offset back to the kit, and a mouse user is not scrolled about. The default layout still gives a list its whole height. (2) No icon tile when no row of the list has a picture (`RowLook::bare`); the name starts at the left. (3) A row's `detail2` (view JSON key) is a second numbers column at the right end, with `detail` before it. Each column is as wide as its widest entry in the list, so the columns line up (`RowLook::columns`). (4) `stat_block` takes `"style": "muted"`: both columns dim. (5) A new component `heading` with the region key `text` (fixed words, no bind; gold, display face, one line). `text` on any other component, or a heading without it, is refused. Region ids stay `f_<field>`. Authoring page `engine/docs/authoring/screen_layouts.md` updated.
- **Tests**: `aegis_ui/tests/layout_kit2.rs` (4). A controls-shaped view (24 bindings) goes through a layout with a 60-unit list region. Every row id exists and row 20 carries its action. Scrolled to the end, a click at row 20 hits row 20. A focused row 20 and its neighbours come into view, and back at row 0 the list returns to the top. A list with room has no scroll area. The new keys are parsed or refused, `detail2` round-trips, and a bare row starts with its text. The test builds its own view because the game's fixture has 7 rows and engine tests name no game. Review render: Art/UI's draft with a 40% list region, headings over both lists, muted fixed inputs and the fixture's key and pad split into the two columns; it scrolls and lines up. Goldens unchanged.
- **For Art/UI (AI-27)**: the draft can now use `"h"` shorter than the list, `{"component": "heading", "text": "Fixed inputs"}` and `"style": "muted"` on `fixed`. For the two columns, the screen's view must give `detail2`; today Settings puts "Enter · Pad A" in one `detail`. Splitting it in `emberwake_gui` is a one-line change for main Build when the layout lands.
- **Guesses**: one row of margin around the focus; the heading uses the body size in the display face; a column is as wide as its longest entry, so one long "Press a key or button…" widens the key column for every row.
- **Also changed**: `emberwake_gui/src/controls_view.rs` builds its rows with `detail2: String::new()` (the new field; no behaviour change).
- **Docs delta**: none beyond the engine authoring page. `HISTORY.md`: none.

### FB-355: ENGINE-19 layout parts for a shop-like screen landed; PR7-39 Stage B can go ahead

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §3 `ENGINE-19` (LAYOUT-KIT3) (@squash `ENGINE-19`)
- **Built** (`aegis_ui::screen_layout`, `panes`): (1) Row `buttons` (`[{"action", "label", "enabled"}]`), drawn at the row's right end, each a widget `<row widget id>.<action>` running that view action with the row's id. A button is off when it says so, its row is off or the view's action is off; every row keeps the widest row's button room free so the numbers line up. (2) Row `selected` draws the selected fill (the widget is active). (3) Row `tone`, a theme colour role (`theme::ROLES`) for `detail`; an unknown role is refused when the view parses. `RowLook` gains `tone`. (4) `list_row` bind `then`: a second rows field under a divider in the same scroll area, dimmed and never clicked, widgets `<screen>.<region>.then.<i>`. (5) A `detail_line` component (bind `text` optional) shows the note (row `note`) of the row under the pointer, else the focused row's, else its text; it draws after every list, so it shows this frame's row, and `Drawn::hot` gives the screen that row's widget id and note. (6) Region key `row_ids` on a `list_row`: `true` gives `<screen>.row.<id>`, a prefix gives `<prefix>.<id>`; two lists may not share one. COMPONENTS has 15 entries.
- **Tests**: `aegis_ui/tests/layout_kit3.rs` (4), on a shop-shaped view: ids and buttons with their actions, off states, the selected row, the dimmed section; foe-coloured pixels only on the toned row; the detail line by pointer, focus and fallback; the JSON round trip and the refusals. ### FB-363: PR7-34 AMBIENCE1, an ambience bus with its own loop channel and the Ward Ambience slider

- **Status**: open
- **Spec**: `READY.md` §1 `PR7-34` (`AMBIENCE1`), `FB-308`'s answer (@squash `PR7-34`)
- **Built** (engine, `aegis_ui::audio`): `Bus::Ambience` with the settings key `ambience` (0-100, default 80 in `Settings::engine_defaults`, master and mute apply). `Audio::ambience(rel)` / `wanted_ambience()`: one loop wanted at a time on its own channel, crossfaded (1 s, 2 s from silence) and looped (loop points as for music), at the music's -6 dB. A music change never cuts the ambience and a place change never cuts the music. `Screen::ambience()` is chosen like `Screen::music()`: the topmost screen's wish, None lets the screen below choose, `Some("")` is silence. The shell applies it each frame beside the music; the agent link's state shows `ambience`. A later bundle part (web) starts a wanted loop whose file was missing, as for music.
- **Game** (`emberwake_gui`): `music::game_ambience(cx, ctx)` takes the first key of the music's context chain (`candidates`: `<region>_<ctx>`, ..., `<world>`, `<ctx>`, then the parent context) that has `audio/ambience/<key>.ogg`. The region map uses its music context (location kind, or shop, which falls back to town) and the world map uses `travel`. Battle, the run-over screen and the epilogue are silent; story screens and menus leave the place's loop playing under them. Sound tab: "Ward Ambience" (the settings mock's row and help line) below Interface Volume. Its sample is `sfx/ui_confirm.wav` on the ambience bus. The Battle tab's Advanced header was already in place (PR7-26 row, its test passes).
- **Ambience keys** (placeholder-first): four placeholder loops in the kit, `kits/rpg/assets/audio/ambience/field.ogg`, `town.ogg`, `travel.ogg` and `danger.ogg`. Each is 8 s of seamless filtered noise (wind, murmur, road wind, low rumble with drips), Ogg Vorbis at about 20 KB, made with numpy and ffmpeg. Every region and hub context reaches one of them: `shop` falls back to `town`, and `danger`, `town` and `travel` fall back to `field`. For AI-30, Art/UI can replace these in place or add game loops in `games/emberwake/assets/audio/ambience/` under the music's keys, such as `sunk_ward_town.ogg`, `sunk_ward.ogg` or `ashlands.ogg`. The game's file wins over the kit's. No README was added under `assets/` because those belong to Art/UI; the folder needs one.
- **Tests**: `aegis_ui` audio unit test (levels, mute, the loop beside the music); `emberwake_gui` `menus` GUI audit (slider below Interface on the full screen and the popup, saved at once, the ambience bus follows and the music does not); `music` every shipped sound decodes (now the `ambience` folder too) and every region and hub context has an ambience loop.
- **Guesses**: (1) Ambience is silent in battle, and battle music plays alone. (2) Ambience keeps playing under story vignettes. A vignette's own ambience key could come later. (3) The ambience level uses the music's -6 dB.
- **Docs delta**: `GAME_BRIEF` audio line: "Ambience: `audio/ambience/<key>.ogg` by the music's keys, on its own bus (Ward Ambience)". `docs/specs/ASSETORG2.md` section 3 tree: `audio/ambience/<key>.ogg` beside `audio/music/` (the layered-tree test now allows it). `HISTORY.md`: none.
